body:
﻿ Federal Reserve Board - Federal Reserve Board announces pricing, effective January 1, 2027, for payment services the Federal Reserve Banks provide to banks and credit unions, and changes to streamline and adjust their check services Skip to main content An official website of the United States Government Here's how you know Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( Lock Locked padlock icon ) or https:// means you've safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites.           the nation with a safe, flexible, and stable monetary and financial
          system. Main Menu Toggle Button Sections Search Toggle Button Search Search Submit Button Submit Home News & Events Press Releases Press Release November 12, 2026 Federal Reserve Board announces pricing, effective January 1, 2027, for payment services the Federal Reserve Banks provide to banks and credit unions, and changes to streamline and adjust their check services For release at 1:30 p.m. EST Share The Federal Reserve Board on Thursday announced pricing, effective January 1, 2027, for payment services the Federal Reserve Banks provide to banks and credit unions, such as the clearing of checks, automated clearing house (ACH) transactions, instant payments, and wholesale payment and settlement services. By law, the Federal Reserve must establish fees to recover the costs, including imputed costs, of providing payment services over the long run. The Federal Reserve expects to recover 101.5 percent of actual and imputed expenses in 2027, including the return on equity that would have been earned if a private-sector firm provided the services. Overall, price changes for 2027 will result in an estimated 1.4 percent average price increase for established, mature services. In addition, the Federal Reserve Banks announced changes to streamline and adjust their check services. As described in the request for information on check services issued last year, the volume of checks processed by the Federal Reserve Banks is declining, but checks remain an important payment instrument for many consumers and businesses. The changes were informed by public feedback and ensure that the Federal Reserve Banks continue to provide check services efficiently. The adjustments include optimizing check processing windows during low-volume periods, increasing fees that banks and credit unions pay to process checks, and other operational updates. These changes do not impact consumers' and businesses' ability to pay with or receive checks and only impact how banks and credit unions process checks with Federal Reserve Banks. The entire 2027 fee schedule for all of the Federal Reserve's payment services is published on FRBservices.org ® . Additional information on the Federal Reserve's payments services, including service usage statistics, is available on the Board's website . For media inquiries, please email [email protected] or call 202-452-2955. Board memo (PDF) Federal Register notice (PDF) Last Update:
            November 12, 2026

Main Menu Toggle Button Sections Search Toggle Button Search Search Submit Button Submit Home News & Events Press Releases Press Release November 12, 2026 Federal Reserve announces revised tentative schedule of Federal Open Market Committee meetings in 2027 For release at 12:45 p.m. EST Share The Federal Reserve on Thursday announced a revised tentative schedule of Federal Open Market Committee meetings in 2027. The Committee plans to meet on the dates listed below to discuss monetary policy and will announce its policy decision as usual on the second day of each meeting, except the October 26-27 meeting. That meeting will be dedicated to the discussion of broad monetary policy strategy issues: January 26-27 (Tuesday-Wednesday) March 16-17 (Tuesday-Wednesday) April 27-28 (Tuesday-Wednesday) June 8-9 (Tuesday-Wednesday) July 27-28 (Tuesday-Wednesday) September 14-15 (Tuesday-Wednesday) October 26-27 (Tuesday-Wednesday) November 16-17 (Tuesday-Wednesday) January 25-26, 2028 (Tuesday-Wednesday) For media inquiries, please e-mail [email protected] or call (202) 452-2955 Last Update:

title: From AI ambition to business impact
body: From AI ambition to business impact Nov 12, 2026 | Rodrigo Kede Lima - President, Microsoft Frontier Company Most business leaders I meet no longer need to be convinced that AI works. They’ve seen the pilots, the demos and the copilots. The question I hear in boardrooms now is different: How do we move from AI that impresses to AI that changes how the business actually runs? That is the question Microsoft Frontier Company was built to answer, and to date, we have engaged on nearly 500 projects with over 200 customers across 28 countries. Customers including 3M, Alaska Airlines, BMW, Core42, KT, Land O’Lakes, London Stock Exchange Group, Mastercard, McKesson, Northern Trust, Novo Nordisk, Publicis Groupe, Saint-Gobain, Siemens and Unilever are seeing real value from working side by side with our Forward Deployed Engineering teams. More importantly, most customers where we have completed initial projects have returned for additional engagements, generating hundreds of follow-on projects. Customers don’t come back for engineers. They come back because the first engagement delivered something they could measure and they can see the next workflow worth redesigning. The technology is ready. What slows AI down is everything around it. That means identifying where AI can deliver the greatest value, building in trust and governance, redesigning the operating models and helping people work in new ways. Technology and people have to move forward together. What this looks like in practice Unilever is collaborating with Microsoft engineers to bring AI into its factories. On the factory floor, intelligent technology helps teams boost efficiency and deliver superior products to customers. In Pondicherry factory — Unilever’s largest Home Care Liquids factory in South Asia and a 2026 World Economic Forum Lighthouse site — a digital twin built on NVIDIA Omniverse and hosted on Azure simulates a real factory environment with integrated live data. This helps anticipate issues before they occur, monitors performance in real time and guides operators through the fixes and recommendations. 3M is working with our engineers to help its Global Business Services team automate customer order management. The companies are building an AI agent-driven workflow to assist with credit checks, delinquency assessments and system updates, with human-in-the-loop controls and a custom monitoring dashboard for real-time visibility and approvals. The solution is expected to significantly reduce manual effort, improve speed and consistency and accelerate cash flow — freeing staff for higher-value work while enabling scalable, auditable operations. Publicis Groupe is co-building with our engineers to bring AI into the heart of how it works and delivers for clients. Microsoft engineers work side by side with Publicis teams to design and build agentic processes grounded in Microsoft IQ, so agents work with the business context, data and knowledge behind Publicis’ work. These processes use reinforcement learning, drawing on real-world outcomes and human feedback to keep improving how the agents perform over time. The approach combines very fast engineering with hands-on knowledge transfer, helping Publicis build lasting AI capability. The work builds on Publicis’ rollout of Microsoft 365 Copilot to all 114,000 of its employees. Northern Trust needed to accelerate onboarding to its Asset Servicing Front Office Solutions platform, a process that took about two and a half weeks per client. Our engineers worked alongside Northern Trust’s experts to build an AI-powered onboarding agent within the Excel and SharePoint tools analysts already use. The result: data preparation time fell 83%, from two and a half weeks to three days, with 96.5% first pass quality score in testing . Analysts remain in control while gaining more time for higher-value client service. KT , one of South Korea’s largest telecommunications providers, wanted to help network operators identify and respond to problems faster. Our engineers worked from KT’s offices to co-build AIO-Net, a continuously learning AI agent platform informed by KT’s operating procedures and veteran network experts. It now detects network issues in two to three minutes, down from more than ten, while keeping people in control of decisions and actions. Saint-Gobain , the 360-year-old construction materials company, is using AI to help reduce the carbon footprint of cement. Working alongside its researchers, Microsoft engineers used Microsoft Discovery to gather 62,000 patents and 44,000 research abstracts into a knowledge base in hours, work Saint-Gobain estimates would have taken researchers a year. In about six weeks, the team identified new hypotheses for cement additives that scientists are now testing in the lab. Across all of these customers, the pattern is the same: Begin with the value , not the technology. Redesign the process , not just the task. Build in fast cycles with the customer’s teams. Put security, governance and cost management in place from day one , so scaling doesn’t stall. This is how organizations move from isolated AI projects to sustainable transformation: by focusing on measurable outcomes, redesigning work and building the capabilities to keep improving over time. New research from IDC underscores why this approach matters. While 66% of organizations report substantial or transformative results from AI, only 48% are scaling or seeing consistent value across their organizations. At the same time, 71% expect AI spending to increase by at least 10% in the next year, putting even greater pressure on businesses to demonstrate measurable returns. The challenge is no longer simply adopting AI. It is reimagining how work gets done and turning that transformation into lasting business impact. We’re holding ourselves to the same standard If we’re asking customers to redesign how they work around AI, we have to do the same. Microsoft Frontier Company was deliberately designed to be flat and fast, with one front door for customers, and as a reference for what an AI-native organization can look like. We are learning, adjusting and moving fast, the same way we ask our customers to. The real measure of success The gap between AI that impresses and AI that delivers won’t close on its own. It closes workflow by workflow, with people who understand the business sitting next to people who can build. Our success will be measured by more than what we deliver. The real test is what our customers can do after we’ve worked together: run, govern and improve their own AI systems, on their terms, with their intelligence protected. Their success is the clearest measure of ours. Learn more at www.microsoft.com/en-us/frontier-company . Rodrigo Kede Lima is the President of Microsoft Frontier Company and leads the operating business of 6,000 industry and engineering experts focused on delivering Frontier Transformation through AI for customers around the world. NOTE IDC Infographic, sponsored by Microsoft, The Real Business Value of AI, IDC #US54985026-IG, November 2026 Tags: AI , Azure , Microsoft 365 Copilot , Microsoft Frontier Company

title: We're launching a $10 million Energy Impact Program in West Virginia.
body: We're launching a $10 million Energy Impact Program in West Virginia. Nov 12, 2026 Today, we’re announcing a $10 million Energy Impact Program to support energy innovation and affordability in West Virginia. The first $1 million will go toward the West Virginia Office of Energy across six counties: Putnam, Kanawha, Cabell, Mason, Jackson, and Lincoln. Many older homes require basic repairs — like fixing roof leaks or outdated wiring — before they qualify for energy upgrades. This funding covers those essential repairs, helping qualifying families access the state Home Energy Rebate program to lower their monthly utility bills. Additionally, local governments and nonprofits will receive funding through the EECBG program for lighting, insulation, and HVAC upgrades, allowing them to redirect utility savings back into local services. This initiative is an early step in Google’s long-term investment in the communities near its planned Buffalo data center campus. To check eligibility and apply, visit energywv.org .

We are awarding $13 million to 148 graduate students through our 2026 PhD Fellowship Program. These researchers are studying ways to improve medical imaging, create inclusive language tools, and design faster computer hardware. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer Today, we are announcing the recipients of the 2026 Google PhD Fellowship Program . This year, Google.org is providing $13 million in funding to support fellowship recipients, including 148 new PhD fellows across 38 countries, deepening our commitment to the early-career scientists who are advancing the "science of AI" for the public good. The 2026 Google PhD Fellowship cohort has broad global reach, with representation across 38 countries. Foundational science with global reach Every transformative leap in technology begins the same way: with a researcher asking a bold, foundational question long before the rest of the world sees the answer. What makes this cohort extraordinary isn’t just the technical depth of their work, but the global reach and real-world ambition behind it. Around the world, these fellows are tackling problems that matter to communities everywhere: Accelerating health and life sciences: From developing representation-learning frameworks in Brazil that integrate complex genetic data to uncover disease causes, to making medical-imaging neural networks more interpretable and reliable in South Africa. Building inclusive, resilient systems: From advancing natural language processing and speech recognition for Nigerian languages, to co-designing accessible security and privacy tools for Deaf and hard-of-hearing communities in Germany. Pushing the frontiers of AI and computer hardware: From designing faster microchips that process data more efficiently in Taiwan, to creating reliable, step-by-step reasoning for language models and testing quantum theory in the lab. Direct funding and lifelong community Breakthrough science rarely happens in isolation. Beyond direct funding and access to compute which gives students the freedom to pursue high-risk, high-reward ideas, every fellow gains access to engage with Google researchers, and is welcomed into a global scientific peer network. Since 2009, the PhD Fellowship Program has supported more than 1,100 graduate students worldwide. Over the past 17 years, we have seen firsthand where that early catalyst can lead. Alumni of the program are now tenured professors, startup founders, open-source pioneers, and research leaders helping shape technology at Google itself. When we support foundational science and the emerging researchers brave enough to chart the unknown, we help build a stronger, more representative global scientific landscape for everyone. title: Scientists are using Google AI to help restore giant kelp forests.
body: Scientists are using Google AI to help restore giant kelp forests. Nov 12, 2026 Underwater forests of giant kelp protect coastlines, provide habitat, and support marine ecosystems — but they’re disappearing worldwide due to ocean warming. As COP31 kicks off this week, we’re sharing results from our partnership with Australia's national science agency, CSIRO , which is using AI and genomics to help restore giant kelp . The team recently published two high-quality reference genomes for Australian giant kelp, providing a foundation for conservation genetics work. Next researchers trained a version of Google's open-source AI tool DeepVariant to analyze giant kelp DNA. It sequenced 600 wild specimens collected from 40 sites along the Tasmanian coast, where populations have dwindled to 5% of historic numbers. This video explains how the genetic analysis and partners’ lab-based cross-breeding studies are laying the groundwork for a real-world outcome: giant kelp forests replanted with diverse, heat-tolerant specimens. This effort is part of Google Australia's Digital Futures Initiative .

title: Scaling AI value without losing control: Lessons from Frontier Firms
body: Scaling AI value without losing control: Lessons from Frontier Firms Nov 12, 2026 | Alysa Taylor - Chief Marketing Officer, Commercial Cloud & AI Results are widespread. Value at scale is not, and that gap is what this year’s research from IDC , commissioned by Microsoft, set out to explain. In our fourth year commissioning IDC, more than 5,200 senior IT and business leaders across 28 industries shared what it takes to maximize value as AI scales. The clearest lessons come from Frontier Firms, the group last year’s research introduced: the top 10% of organizations on IDC’s AI maturity scale. What the research found Frontier Firms lead on return. They report an average 4x return on AI versus 2.7x for slow adopters (the bottom 30% on IDC’s scale), and 39% see returns of 5x or more versus 4% of slow adopters. Measurement is the next test . Only 61% of organizations are highly confident they can measure AI’s business value and ROI, versus 93% of Frontier Firms. Governance is in place, but confidence lags. 65% of organizations have an established process to govern agents, yet only 60% have high confidence in addressing AI security and governance risks. Workforce readiness is uneven. 67% say their workforce reports high trust in AI, yet only 20% have a comprehensive, organization-wide skilling strategy. “Organizations that scale AI value aren’t simply spending more. They manage AI investments, models, agents, governance and skills as one discipline, and that is what turns early results into value they can repeat across the business,” says Kathy Lange, Research Director, AI, Data and Automation Software, IDC. AI value now reaches well beyond cost savings Organizations now use AI in 6.5 business areas on average, led by IT infrastructure, cybersecurity and customer service, with the fastest growth in industry-specific uses. Employee experience, revenue growth, customer experience, innovation and risk reduction now rank nearly even as the places AI strengthens the business. Cost is an important consideration, but it is evaluated alongside accuracy, security, compliance and scalability. Where scale stalls 66% of leaders say AI has delivered substantial or transformative results, but only 48% are scaling that value across multiple business units. Agents follow the same pattern: 36% of organizations are still piloting them. The widest gap is people: workforce confidence is running well ahead of the plans to support it. The organizations pulling ahead are closing these gaps by design. Inside the Frontier Firm IDC’s maturity scale weighs spending discipline, breadth of use, agent adoption, skills, confidence in managing AI risk and outcomes. On agents specifically, Frontier Firms report a 3.8x return versus 3.0x for slow adopters. These returns are leader-reported, and the research shows association rather than cause. What they do differently comes down to five behaviors: They invest ahead of plan . 90% of Frontier Firms exceeded their planned AI spend. They deploy AI broadly , across most of the business, not just a few teams. They put agents to work . 96% are rolling out agents at scale, and 53% orchestrate them across workflows. They govern so they can scale . 87% have a process to govern and oversee agents, versus 51% of slow adopters. They build skills everywhere . 80% have an organization-wide AI skilling strategy, versus 3% of slow adopters. At Bristol Myers Squibb , the RABIT agent “connects the dots across meetings, helping teams make better decisions while reducing administrative follow-up work,” says Lakshman Yerramalla, Director of Portfolio Governance and Delivery for Global Manufacturing Operations. Project managers who use it save up to an estimated 20% of their time. Four disciplines for scaling AI value The lesson from Frontier Firms is one I believe every leader can act on: scaling AI value means managing models, agents, governance and measurement as one accountable system. Value and control aren’t a trade-off. I see the same pattern with customers: the organizations scaling fastest treat AI as a change in how the business runs, not a technology rollout. “The skilling that a lot of companies miss is the business skilling,” says Eric Tabor, Chief Digital Officer, KOHLER . “We also focus on how to dissect processes and convert them into AI workflows.” Unlock model choice Trust and security, leading-edge technology and model performance tie as the top criteria for choosing an AI platform (44% each). Match the right model to each job, balancing cost with protection of intellectual property and data. Redesign workflows around agents Agents create the most value when work is redesigned around them. The bigger opportunity is what they free people to do more of: leaders point to creativity, innovation and business reinvention (41%), customer-facing work and relationships (39%) and analytical work and data interpretation (39%). Connect agents across processes, with human oversight where it matters. Govern decisions and actions Trust is building faster than confidence. Most leaders report high trust in their AI systems, yet fewer are highly confident addressing security and governance risks. As agents take on more of the work, trust has to be earned continuously, and governance has to reach beyond models to keep people in control of what agents decide and do. Conagra Brands made governance its starting point. “Laying the foundation of proper governance, observability and responsible AI was our first step to engaging our employees with AI,” says Tracy Schaefer, Chief Information Officer, Conagra Brands. “We built a SteerCo to review risk factors, access and identity management.” Measure and optimize value Connect investment and performance data to business outcomes, compare how processes perform before and after AI and direct spending where it delivers the most value. With 71% of organizations expecting AI budgets to rise 10% or more in the next 12 months, this discipline will separate leaders from the rest. Underneath all four disciplines are people. None of it scales without an organization-wide plan to build AI skills. That’s where Frontier Firms are furthest ahead, and it’s where I’d urge every leader to start. Black & Veatch reached 98% adoption of Microsoft 365 Copilot through deliberate change management, including early-adopter cohorts that surfaced real business use cases. “Our goal is to be a Frontier Firm. The intention is not to stop at pure adoption,” says Mike Adams, Chief Digital Technology Officer, Black & Veatch. Go deeper at Microsoft Ignite IDC Executive Analyst Shari Lava will lead three sessions at Microsoft Ignite on Nov. 18, including The AI ROI Divide: Why Some Organizations Scale and Others Stall. What this means for business The gap that matters now isn’t between companies that use AI and those that don’t. It’s between those getting results in pockets and those turning AI into repeatable value across the business. There are three key ways leaders can step into this kind of transformation. First, treat AI as business transformation, not a technology rollout. Frontier Firms connect AI to the outcomes that matter most, from growth to customer experience, and manage it as one accountable system. That is the heart of Frontier Transformation, and it’s the work we’re doing alongside our customers every day. Second, start with your own function. In marketing, we’re applying these same disciplines to our own work: redesigning workflows around agents, setting clear guardrails and measuring what AI actually delivers. Every function can become its own proof point for the rest of the business. Third, invest in people as much as in technology. Skills are the widest gap in this year’s research, and it’s the one I care about most. The organizations that pull ahead will be the ones where everyone, at every level, has the support to learn, experiment and grow with AI. The next phase of AI won’t be defined by who uses it. It will be defined by who can scale its value and stay in control. This research gives every leader a benchmark for where they stand today and a clear view of what to do next. Get the full picture Download the global infographic , The Real Business Value of AI, to see a summary of findings and benchmark your organization against Frontier Firms before your next AI investment review. Regional infographics are also available for Europe , Asia Pacific and the Americas . The full InfoBrief will follow. Alysa Taylor is the Chief Marketing Officer for Commercial Cloud and AI at Microsoft, leading teams that enable digital and AI transformation for organizations of all sizes across the globe. title: A New Dawn in the Cloud: ‘Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV’ Is Coming to GeForce NOW
body: A New Dawn in the Cloud: ‘Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV’ Is Coming to GeForce NOW Plus, catch NVIDIA DLSS 5 updates for ‘War Thunder’ and ‘Where Winds Meet,’ and dive into ‘Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen,’ alongside 10 new games. November 12, 2026 by GeForce NOW Community 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Rally the ranks this GFN Thursday. Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV is coming to GeForce NOW , allowing players to experience the battle for Kronus through cloud gaming. There’s more on the horizon, with NVIDIA DLSS 5 technology coming to War Thunder and Where Winds Meet . Meanwhile, Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen brings new tales and encounters, alongside 10 games joining the GeForce NOW library this week. Kronus Calls for Reinforcements Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV , developed by KING Art Games and published by Deep Silver, is coming to GeForce NOW. Launching on Steam Thursday, Dec. 3, the real-time strategy game returns to the series’ roots with large-scale battles, base building and a renewed fight for planet Kronus. Command the Space Marines, Orks, Necrons or the Adeptus Mechanicus, which makes their series debut. Build a base, secure resources and customize squads to the conflict across more than 70 campaign missions, playable solo or in co-op mode. The Last Stand, Skirmish and multiplayer modes offer more ways to put tactics to the test. GeForce NOW will bring the action to supported PCs, Macs, handhelds and other devices, with game downloads and updates handled in the cloud. Save the storage space for everyday essentials and planning for the next offensive. Wishlist the game on Steam , and stay tuned to GFN Thursday to prepare for launch. DLSS 5 Keeps on Coming NVIDIA DLSS 5 continues to evolve, with Gaijin Entertainment’s War Thunder and Everstone Studio’s Where Winds Meet next to receive support for the technology with the 3D-Guided Neural Rendering feature. Arriving in mid-November, War Thunder ’s Eagle’s Shadow major update adds DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, dozens of new planes, ships and tanks, along with cluster bombs for planes and visual-effects enhancements increasing the realism and dynamism of battle. In Where Winds Meet , DLSS support arrives Monday, Nov. 23, enhancing the environments and characters of its wuxia open-world action role-playing game. Both titles will use the latest DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering model, released in October, which doubles model performance compared with the previous version. Since its initial announcement in March, model performance has improved tenfold, bringing the technology to more gamers, including GeForce NOW Ultimate members streaming with GeForce RTX 5080 cloud rigs. Get a closer look at the DLSS updates and find more details . A New Tale for the Arisen Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen is streaming on GeForce NOW, expanding the deep, explorable fantasy world of Dragon’s Dogma 2 with new tales and encounters. Travel to the long-abandoned region of Norgan, join the enigmatic Eir and uncover the secrets of the undying Fallen Dragon. Unearth forgotten relics to unlock powerful weapons and skills, take on Lost Rites’ 12 dungeon challenges and explore new hairstyles and tattoos for Arisen and Pawn customization. Delicious in Dungeon also arrives in the world of Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen with a special collaboration. GeForce NOW keeps all the new downloadable content available across supported devices — without a single download claiming local storage on a gamer’s hardware of choice. In addition, members can look for the following games joining the GeForce NOW library this week: Worst Class Ever (New release on Steam , Nov. 9) Ashes of the Singularity II (New release on Steam , Nov. 10) Cyberpunk 2077 ( Xbox Play Anywhere, new release on Battle.net , Nov. 10) DreamWorks Shrek 2 Remastered (New release on Steam , Nov. 10) Warhammer Survivors (New release on Steam and Xbox , available on Game Pass, Nov. 10) Main Sequence (New release on Steam , Nov. 12) Deadly Days: Roadtrip ( Steam ) GeForce 8800 GTX – 20 Years of a Legend ( Steam , Ultimate members) Graveyard Keeper ( Steam ) Tape to Tape ( Steam ) Also this week, Ultimate members can take a trip back to 2006 with GeForce 8800 GTX – 20 Years of a Legend , a playable demo celebrating the iconic GPU’s 20th anniversary with DLSS 4.5 and path tracing in the cloud. Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after release and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates on announced titles. Those ready to put the next game plan into action can grab a day pass to try Performance or Ultimate, with the cost applicable toward a first monthly membership. What’s on the gaming lineup this weekend? Let us know on X or in the comments below. body: See our intelligent eyewear lineup and pre-order your pair Nov 12, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Designed in collaboration with Warby Parker, Gentle Monster, and Samsung, intelligent eyewear gives you hands-free help from Gemini when you're on the go. Shahram Izadi VP & GM, XR Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Listen to article [[duration]] minutes This content is generated by Google AI. These frames integrate Gemini to provide hands-free assistance, real-time translations, and visual descriptions throughout your day. You can visit the Gentle Monster, Warby Parker, or Google Store websites to place your order or find a location to try on a pair before the December 10 launch. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Shahram Izadi, VP and GM of XR, announced that pre-orders for new Intelligent Eyewear are now open. These frames integrate Gemini to provide hands-free assistance, real-time translations, and navigation through your daily tasks. You can choose from stylish designs by Gentle Monster and Warby Parker that work with your phone. The glasses feature a twelve-megapixel camera, nine hours of battery life, and built-in privacy protection controls. You can purchase these frames online or in stores starting on December 10 of this year. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Shahram Izadi, VP and GM of XR, explains that our new Intelligent Eyewear collections from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker bring Gemini directly to your frames. These lightweight glasses help you navigate your day hands-free by providing real-time directions, language translations, and visual assistance. You can also capture photos, listen to music, and manage your schedule while keeping your phone in your pocket. Pre-orders are open now, and the glasses arrive in stores on December 10. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer Today, pre-orders begin for the new Intelligent Eyewear collections, made in collaboration with Gentle Monster, Warby Parker, and Samsung. With help from Gemini, these frames are ready to bring you real-time assistance throughout your day, right when you need it. 1 The new Intelligent Eyewear collections These collections, which were designed to fit a variety of styles, integrate helpful technology into frames you’ll want to wear every day, and work with Pixel and Samsung phones, as well as iPhones. 2 Gentle Monster’s high-end designs transform glasses into a means of self-expression. Their Intelligent Eyewear Collection includes six designs in bold colors — including dark red, pink, gray, and yellow — paired with tinted, clear, blue, or brown lenses. Prescription options are available for most frames. Starting at $449, the collection will be available in the United States and in South Korea. Warby Parker’s Intelligent Eyewear lineup features three refined styles — Alden, Reid, and Wren — inspired by the brand’s most beloved silhouettes, with timeless design and lightweight comfort at the forefront. You can choose from optical or sun styles starting at $395, in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black colorways, with a wide range of prescription, width, and lens options. The full collection is available at warbyparker.com , and customers can sign up for a guided demo experience at more than 360 Warby Parker retail locations. Intelligent eyewear was engineered to be comfortable and helpful all day. The glasses feature lightweight frames (weighing around 41 grams) and a battery that lasts up to nine hours. 3 Each pair comes with a sleek, portable charging case that can recharge your frames up to seven times. 4 A smarter way to see the world Gemini on intelligent eyewear helps connect the dots across the Google apps and services you use every day to get you hands-free help. Just say “Hey Gemini” or tap your frames to learn the story behind a street art mural you are passing by, ask for a tailored recommendation from a “New Arrivals” bookshelf, or look at an event poster to check your Calendar availability on the spot. Gemini also helps handle your busywork in the background. Whether you’re walking between meetings or running errands with your hands full, you can ask Gemini to add what you’re looking at to your grocery list, or remind you where your next meeting is — all while keeping your eyes up and your day moving. When you’re exploring somewhere new, Google Maps delivers turn-by-turn directions in your ear. And when you ask Gemini, Google Translate will deliver real-time speech translation with automatic language detection across more than 70 languages. The glasses also feature Gemini’s new Guided Vision , which offers conversational audio descriptions to people who are blind, have low vision, or want intuitive visual assistance as they read small print or find everyday items. 5 And thanks to our collaboration with Aira , users can say “Hey Gemini, open Aira Explorer” to stream their glasses' camera feed directly to a professionally trained human visual interpreter for real-time support. Never miss a moment Custom-tuned open-ear speakers direct clear vocals and balanced audio right into your ear while keeping you fully aware of what’s around you. You can soundtrack your day with YouTube Music, Spotify, or Apple Music, and jump back into your audiobook on Audible. 6 Or use your glasses to catch up on your missed group chats, respond to messages, and take phone calls hands-free. With the integrated 12-megapixel ultra-wide camera, capturing high-quality photos and videos is as simple as pressing a button — or just asking Gemini. Your phone stays in your pocket so you can capture the moment while staying in it. HDR processing and image stabilization ensure your images and videos stay crisp, vibrant, and steady, while spatial audio capture helps you relive the moments like you were there. Privacy designed for both sides of the lens When technology can see the world around you, it has a responsibility to the people around you, too. We set out to design intelligent eyewear so that personal help doesn’t come at the expense of anyone’s privacy. You can read about our approach to privacy on intelligent eyewear in our blog , and learn more about privacy features on the Google Safety Center . Key protections include: Camera visuals from Gemini on glasses are not saved in your Gemini History and aren’t used to train AI models or target ads. Your glasses are also designed to automatically redact bystanders’ faces from these visuals before Gemini processes them. Data stored on glasses is encrypted, and if data leaves your glasses, it’s also encrypted in transit to keep it private and secure. You control which apps access your glasses’ camera and mic, and you can change these permissions whenever you like. You can also review or delete your chats with Gemini, and adjust your settings at any time in Gemini History. When you take a photo or video for your gallery, an indicator light lets people around you know. The glasses are designed to stop recording if the light is covered or disabled. Every pair has an off switch so you can turn your glasses completely off whenever you want to wear them as regular glasses only. Pre-orders are live online and in-store at Gentle Monster and Warby Parker. Hands-on demos are also available at select Gentle Monster, Warby Parker, and Google Store locations. Intelligent eyewear will be available to purchase in stores and online on December 10. Learn more at glasses.google . title: Designing for privacy on intelligent eyewear
body: Designing for privacy on intelligent eyewear Nov 12, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Our new intelligent eyewear can give you fast answers about what you see, all while staying hands free. Learn more about how we’re building eyewear designed to protect the privacy of you and the people around you. Shahram Izadi VP & GM, XR Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Listen to article [[duration]] minutes This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Read AI-generated summary Shahram Izadi, VP and GM of XR, explains how we are building privacy protections into intelligent eyewear to safeguard both wearers and bystanders. These features include physical indicator lights, automatic face redaction, and strict data encryption to ensure your information remains secure. You can visit the Google Safety Center to learn more about our approach to privacy and how we handle data across our wearable devices. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Shahram Izadi, VP and GM of XR, explains how we prioritize privacy for both wearers and bystanders. We do not save camera visuals in Gemini History, nor do we use them for model training. You control your data through app permissions, chat history settings, and a physical power off switch. An outward LED indicator light alerts people nearby when you capture photos or record video footage. Our glasses automatically redact faces and use directional microphones to focus solely on your own voice. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Shahram Izadi, VP and GM of XR, explains that our intelligent eyewear uses Gemini to help you translate signs, read menus, and navigate your day. We built these glasses with privacy for everyone in mind, including physical indicator lights for bystanders and automatic face redaction. Your visual data is encrypted, never used for ads, and not saved in your history. You also keep full control over your settings and can turn the device off anytime. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer Intelligent eyewear with Gemini 1 can help you understand another language, make sense of a confusing parking sign, or know when to take the next step in your recipe, all thanks to its ability to see what you see. And with experiences like Guided Vision in Gemini Live , these glasses can provide audio descriptions to people who are blind or have low vision as they read small print or find everyday items. 2 But when technology can see the world around you, it has a responsibility to the people around you, too. Throughout our years of research on glasses, we listened closely to wearers, bystanders, and privacy experts. We found that wearers were constantly calculating using glasses like these out-and-about during their day, while bystanders noted concerns about being filmed without their knowledge. This led us to the conviction that privacy protections on glasses must cover both the person behind the lenses and those in front of them. Privacy designed for both sides of the lens With this in mind, we set out to design the glasses so that personal help doesn’t come at the expense of anyone’s privacy. Here are some of the key features we’ve built into both the hardware and software to protect wearers and those nearby. Protecting your visual data Camera visuals aren’t saved in your Gemini History . When you ask Gemini on glasses about the world around you, like getting help translating a menu in another language, the camera visuals are not saved in your Gemini History. 3 Camera visuals aren’t used for AI training or ad targeting. The visuals Gemini captures are used to give you answers or get you the help you need. They are not used to train AI models or target ads. Your data is encrypted. Data stored on glasses is encrypted, and if data leaves your glasses — like for processing on your phone or in the cloud — it’s also encrypted in transit to keep it private and secure. Coming soon, we’re also bringing Private AI Compute technology to glasses to process data in a secure, fortified space in addition to our other safeguards. You choose what you share You choose what apps can access your camera. Giving apps access to your glasses camera can be really helpful, like if you want to sync your audiobook app with the last page you read in your paperback copy. But before any app can access your camera for the first time, it asks for your permission. After that, you stay in control, and you can grant or revoke access anytime for each individual app. You control your Gemini history. Your chats are saved in Gemini History so you can pick up a conversation where you left off and get more personalized help. You control your personalization and history settings, so you can review past interactions, delete individual chats, or even delete all of them. You can also control in settings whether the text of your chats is used to improve generative AI models. Learn more about how your Gemini data is handled in the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub . Every pair has an off switch. And of course, you have a physical power switch on the frames to turn your glasses completely off whenever you want to wear them as regular glasses only. Privacy protections for those around you Every pair of glasses has an outer indicator light. We’ve heard from bystanders that the most helpful feature for them is a clear indication that the glasses are recording photos and videos. When you take a photo or video for your gallery, an outward-facing LED indicator lights up to let people around you know. The indicator light is designed not to be messed with . If the indicator light is covered or tampered with, sensors are designed to detect that and prevent photos or videos from being taken. The glasses are designed to redact faces before sending images to Gemini. When you ask Gemini a question, there may be others nearby. Not only are these Gemini visuals not used for AI model training, your glasses are also designed to automatically redact bystanders’ faces before Gemini processes the visuals. Gemini is designed to focus on your voice. We’ve also designed Gemini to focus on your voice by default, and not other voices around you, using directional microphones on the glasses. These are a few examples of the privacy features built into the intelligent eyewear experience. Learn more about our approach in the Google Safety Center . Protections and restrictions across Google In addition to these features, there are also protections across Google apps and services to deter misuse of the glasses. Responsible use requirements: Before using intelligent eyewear, users must agree not to record others without permission, not to record in sensitive places, and not to cover the outer indicator light. Not following these requirements is a violation of the Google Terms of Service, and a user’s ability to use the glasses may be disabled. Google Shopping and Google Ads: Policies do not allow the promotion of products and services that disable or hide recording indicator lights on smart glasses. Google Play : Policies prohibit apps from using the camera for social live-streaming or real-time facial identification, and from changing the behavior of the outer indicator light. YouTube: Policies prohibit content that depicts things like harassment and unwanted sexualization. Any video uploaded to YouTube — whether it’s recorded on a phone, a camera, or glasses — has to follow these policies, and videos that don’t are removed. Account restrictions: Intelligent eyewear devices are designed to be set up only with compatible 18+ Google Accounts. This is just the beginning. Privacy is foundational to how we design, build, and evolve wearable technology. As glasses become more capable, our focus is on creating helpful experiences that make both wearers and bystanders feel protected. We look forward to advancing this work in collaboration with privacy experts and others across the ecosystem to further protections for everyone on both sides of the lens. title: We’re introducing a new transparency tool for invalid traffic in Google Ads.
body: Google Ads We’re introducing a new transparency tool for invalid traffic in Google Ads. Keerat Sharma VP & General Manager, Ads Privacy and Safety Nov 12, 2026 We’ve long built defenses directly into our ad systems to block invalid traffic, helping businesses get the most out of their budgets and spend with confidence. Today, we’re rolling out the Invalid Traffic Overview Card in Google Ads to give advertisers front-end transparency into how we protect their campaigns. We don’t charge for invalid traffic, and our multi-layered defenses have always worked in the background to catch it before an advertiser is billed. We issue a credit when it’s detected later, where appropriate and possible. Now, for the first time, businesses can see both the amount saved and the credits we automatically provide for invalid activity in Google Ads. As bad actors become more sophisticated, we’re continually strengthening our approach to keep policy violators off our platforms. So far in 2026, we’ve reduced advertiser exposure to invalid leads by an average of 30% through continuous system upgrades.
retained_feed_body: Google Ads introduces the Invalid Traffic Overview Card for campaign transparency. See your savings and credits from November 2026. Get the details.

title: Champaign County man sentenced to 15 years in prison for distributing child pornography
body: Press Release Champaign County man sentenced to 15 years in prison for distributing child pornography Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Ohio DAYTON, Ohio – Christopher Creamer, 40, of Urbana, was sentenced in U.S. District Court today to 180 months in prison, followed by a 15-year term of supervised release, for distributing child pornography. According to court documents, from June to August 2025, Creamer communicated online with an individual he believed to be a Telegram user but was actually an FBI agent. Creamer distributed two images and 16 videos of child pornography to the agent. He also discussed his interest in the sexual abuse of children. In a subsequent search of Creamer’s electronic devices, agents discovered more than 3,000 images and 130 videos depicting child pornography, including images of the sexual abuse of infants and toddlers and sadomasochistic conduct. Creamer further admitted that he previously sexually abused a 14-year-old victim. Creamer was arrested and charged by federal criminal complaint in March and pleaded guilty in July. Dominick S. Gerace II, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Ohio, and Jason Cromartie, Special Agent in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Cincinnati Division,  announced the sentence imposed today by Senior U.S. District Judge Thomas M. Rose. Assistant United States Attorney Christina E. Mahy is representing the United States in this case. This case is part of Project Safe Childhood , a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by U.S. Attorney’s Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. # # # Updated November 12, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Ohio, Southern

body: Press Release Tallahassee Felon Pleads Guilty to Federal Firearm Offense Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Tallahassee, Florida – Etavious J. Milton, 27, of Tallahassee, Florida, pleaded guilty in federal court to possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. The plea was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “The Tallahassee Police Department deserves particular recognition for taking this dangerous criminal off our streets, and thanks to the successful prosecution by my office we will ensure he remains behind federal bars as long as possible. Our citizens deserve to live in safe, crime-free neighborhoods, and my office will deliver on that promise by incapacitating the dangerous criminals who have preyed upon our communities for far too long.” Court documents reflect that at approximately 3:00 a.m. on January 17, 2026, the defendant attempted to flee from law enforcement after committing a traffic violation. The defendant crashed the vehicle he was driving, after narrowly avoiding hitting another vehicle. While waiting for an ambulance, officers stabilized the defendant and observed a black Beretta 9mm caliber pistol near his waist. The officers secured the firearm, and the defendant was then taken to the hospital after emergency medical personnel arrived on scene.  As a previously convicted felon, the defendant was prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition. Milton faces up to 15 years imprisonment. The case involved a joint investigation by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives and the Tallahassee Police Department. Assistant United States Attorney Eric Welch is prosecuting the case. Sentencing is scheduled for January 22, 2027 at 11:00 a.m. at the United States Courthouse in Tallahassee before United States District Judge Mark Walker. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities . The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access available public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl . title: Firearms Smugglers Sentenced in Del Rio to Combined 39.5 Years in Federal Prison
body: Press Release Firearms Smugglers Sentenced in Del Rio to Combined 39.5 Years in Federal Prison Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Texas DEL RIO, Texas – Two Americans and an illegal alien from Mexico were sentenced in a federal court in Del Rio on Tuesday to a combined 474 months in prison for their roles in a firearms trafficking conspiracy, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas. According to court documents, Edgar Josue Montelongo-Loera, 39, of Dallas, and Reymundo Hernandez-Nino, 41, an illegal alien from Mexico were determined to be responsible for the trafficking of firearms to Mexico. In August 2024, agents from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) received information that Montelongo-Loera’s sister and Hernande-Nino’s wife, Kenia Lizbeth Montelongo, 31, had purchased multiple firearms including seven .380 caliber pistols and a .22 caliber pistol between May 17, 2024, and July 5, 2024. In the days following each of the purchases, Montelongo crossed into Mexico through Laredo. Montelongo-Loera, who had displayed multiple firearms in his social media profile pictures, was also recorded crossing in the same vehicle. USA v. Hernandez-Nino et. al. Case 2:25cr1979 In August 2024, ATF agents reviewed WhatsApp conversations that included Montelongo-Loera, in which he said his “buddy” could get requested firearms and that he had someone who could transport them. ATF agents reviewed additional WhatsApp conversations in November 2024, in which Montelongo-Loera again discussed his firearm trafficking operation. Montelongo-Loera was arrested on July 14, 2025, after a co-conspirator was found attempting to smuggle eight handguns and 19 magazines into Mexico. Two days later, ATF agents, along with the San Antonio Police Department, and ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations, executed a search warrant on the San Antonio residence of Hernandez-Nino. A total of 24 firearms were immediately recovered, to include handguns, AR-15 style assault rifles, and a shotgun. ATF also recovered more than 4,000 rounds of ammunition from the residence and multiple sets of body armor. Based on other evidence obtained during the investigation, ATF determined that the weapons, ammunition and accessories were bound for a Mexican drug cartel. Hernandez-Nino and Kenia Lizbeth Montelongo were arrested during the search. Montelongo-Loera pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to traffic firearms on Feb. 23. On Feb. 26, Hernandez-Nino pleaded guilty to smuggling goods from the United States and alien in possession of a firearm, while Kenia Lizbeth Montelongo pleaded guilty to smuggling goods from the United States and sale or transfer to a prohibited person. On Tuesday, Chief U.S. District Judge Alia Moses sentenced Montelongo-Loera to 180 months in federal prison. Hernandez-Nino and Kenia Montelongo were sentenced to 150 and 144 months, respectively. “These three sentencings bring to a close a massive case involving ten conspirators who smuggled more than 200 weapons into Mexico,” said U.S. Attorney Simmons. “This activity is orchestrated by cartels, and the weapons being trafficked across the border are in direct support of organized criminal activity. Specifically, these weapons are used by cartels to terrorize Mexican citizens and war with law enforcement in an effort to maintain control of drug trafficking and human smuggling routes. These activities ultimately harm American citizens trapped in the prison of addiction and facilitate the movement of illegal aliens with violent criminal history into our country, our cities, and our neighborhoods. My office has a long history of aggressively prosecuting those who smuggle firearms, and we will continue to aggressively prosecute those who violate American laws at the behest of the Mexican cartels.” “This investigation demonstrates ATF’s unwavering commitment to identifying, disrupting, and dismantling firearms trafficking networks that fuel violence across our borders,” said Special Agent in Charge Michael Weddel for ATF Houston. “These defendants played significant roles in a coordinated operation to illegally acquire and traffic firearms intended for a Mexican drug cartel. Through the dedicated work of our special agents and our law enforcement partners, we were able to uncover this operation, seize dozens of firearms, and hold those responsible accountable. ATF will continue to aggressively pursue those who exploit our firearms laws and facilitate the flow of illegal weapons into the hands of criminal organizations.” Assistant U.S. Attorney Brett Miner prosecuted the case. This case was investigated and prosecuted by the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) as part of Operation Take Back America . HSTFs, which were established by President Trump in Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion, are joint operations led by the Department of Justice and the Department of Homeland Security. Operation Take Back America is a nationwide federal initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. ### Contact USATXW.MediaInquiry@usdoj.gov Updated November 12, 2026 Topics Homeland Security Task Force Firearms Offenses Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - Texas, Western

title: California Man Sentenced to 15 Years in Federal Prison  for Conspiracy to Distribute a Controlled Substance
body: Press Release California Man Sentenced to 15 Years in Federal Prison  for Conspiracy to Distribute a Controlled Substance Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of South Dakota RAPID CITY - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that U.S. District Judge Camela T. Theeler has sentenced a Rapid City, South Dakota, man convicted of Conspiracy to Distribute a Controlled Substance.  The sentencing took place on November 10, 2026. Martin Ramirez, 45, was sentenced to 15 years in federal prison, followed by five years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund. Ramirez was indicted for Conspiracy to Distribute a Controlled Substance by a federal grand jury in July 2025.  He pleaded guilty on September 1, 2026. In 2022, Ramirez connected with individuals in western South Dakota to distribute methamphetamine.  He was ultimately responsible for sending or receiving several pounds of methamphetamine and further distributing it to individuals involved in the conspiracy. This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.  Operation Take Back America streamlines efforts and resources from the Department’s Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Forces (OCDETFs) and Project Safe Neighborhood (PSN).  Through PSN, the District of South Dakota seeks to bring together all levels of law enforcement and the communities they serve to reduce gun violence and make our neighborhoods safer for everyone. This case was investigated by the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Unified Narcotics Enforcement Team (UNET), and the Drug Enforcement Administration. UNET is comprised of law enforcement from the Pennington County Sheriff’s Office, the Rapid City Police Department, South Dakota Division of Criminal Investigation, the South Dakota Highway Patrol and the South Dakota National Guard.  Assistant U.S. Attorneys Edward C. Tarbay and Megan Poppen prosecuted the case. Ramirez was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service. Contact usasd.press@usdoj.gov Updated November 12, 2026 Topic Operation Take Back America Component USAO - South Dakota

body: Press Release Navarre Woman Sentenced to Five Years in Federal Prison for Drug Trafficking Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Pensacola, Florida – Loredana Alessandra Bassolino, 38, of Navarre, Florida was sentenced to five years in federal prison after previously pleading guilty to possession with intent to distribute more than 40 grams of fentanyl and more than 5 grams of methamphetamine. The sentence was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “Thanks to the excellent investigative work of the DEA, with support from the Gulf Coast HIDTA and our U.S. Marshals, and this successful prosecution by my office, this drug trafficker will be kept off our streets. President Donald J. Trump and Attorney General Todd Blanche remain fully committed to delivering the safe, drug-free communities that our citizens deserve, and my office will fulfill that promise with aggressive prosecutions like this one to hold the peddlers of deadly drugs accountable.” Court documents reflect that on January 14, 2026, federal agents executed an arrest warrant for Andre Perry at a hotel in Pensacola, Florida. When law enforcement made entry into Perry’s hotel room to effectuate the arrest, they observed drug paraphernalia littered throughout the room, along with a “speed loader” tool used to quickly load ammunition into firearm magazines. Bassolino, another occupant of the hotel room, admitted that narcotics were present and gave consent to search the room. During their search, law enforcement discovered fentanyl, methamphetamine, and a loaded firearm. Both Bassolino and Perry are convicted felons who are legally prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition, with Perry most recently being convicted of possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine and fentanyl and possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine and fentanyl in July 2025. “Fentanyl remains the biggest drug threat facing our country,” said Special Agent in Charge Daniel Escobar, DEA Tampa Field Division. “Our agents and law enforcement partners remain vigilant in the fight to rid our communities of traffickers who distribute this poison to our citizens.” Perry is scheduled for sentencing on February 11, 2027, at 2:00 pm before United States District Judge T. Kent Wetherell, II in Pensacola, Florida. The conviction and sentence were the result of an investigation by the Drug Enforcement Administration with assistance from the United States Marshals Service and the Gulf Coast High Intensity Drug Trafficking Areas (HIDTA) Task Force. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Thomas S.P. Geeker. title: Convicted Felon Sentenced to More than 15 Years in Prison on Drug-Trafficking Charges
Two Co-Defendants Sentenced to a Total of Nearly 13 Years for Unlawful Possession of a Firearm and Ammunition
body: Press Release Two Co-Defendants Sentenced to a Total of Nearly 13 Years for Unlawful Possession of a Firearm and Ammunition Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Gainesville, Florida – Kelvin Quentin Scott Wright, 32, of Gainesville, Florida, was sentenced to four years and nine months of federal imprisonment, and Reginald Duante Davis, 36, of Gainesville, Florida, was sentenced to eight years of federal imprisonment for possession of a firearm and ammunition by a convicted felon. The sentences were announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “This successful prosecution ensures these dangerous, armed criminals will be kept off our streets for several years. Our state and federal law enforcement partners are committed to keeping our communities safe, and my office will continue to back up their efforts with aggressive prosecutions of dangerous criminals to ensure our citizens get the crime-free streets and neighborhoods they deserve.” Court records reflect that on April 12, 2024, Alachua County Sheriff’s Office stopped a vehicle for multiple traffic violations. The driver was Kelvin Wright and his co-defendant Reginald Davis was the front seat passenger. Both defendants are prohibited from possessing a firearm or ammunition as convicted felons. During the probable cause search of the vehicle, a loaded firearm, marijuana, oxycodone, and nearly 28 grams of crack cocaine were located in the center console. The DNA of both defendants was located on the firearm in various locations. “Keeping firearms out of the hands of convicted felons is critical to protecting our communities from more violence,” said FBI Jacksonville Special Agent in Charge Jason Carley. “The FBI will always work closely with our partners to identify repeat offenders and hold them accountable for their actions.  This case highlights the importance of how strong partnerships make a real difference in keeping our communities safe.” “The federal sentencing in this case underscores our commitment to keeping guns out of the hands of convicted felons,” said Alachua County Sheriff Chad D. Scott. “I am grateful for the strong partnership between our deputies, federal agencies, and prosecutors who work together every day to protect the safety of Alachua County.” The case was jointly investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Alachua County Sheriff’s Office. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Christie S. Utt. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities . The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General.  To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl . Sumter Man Sentenced to Federal Prison After Flying Drone Over South Carolina Prison
body: Press Release Sumter Man Sentenced to Federal Prison After Flying Drone Over South Carolina Prison Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of South Carolina COLUMBIA, S.C. — Quinzell Robinson, 47, of Sumter, has been sentenced to one year and one day in federal prison for flying a drone onto a South Carolina prison yard. On March 14, 2025, at 5 a.m., law enforcement responded to reports of a drone flying near Lieber Correctional Facility in Ridgeville. Investigators located Robinson leaving the woods near the facility with a drone and a bag. After reviewing surveillance footage, investigators learned that shortly after 5 a.m., a package was dropped onto prison grounds and retrieved by inmates. Investigators sought and obtained authorization to search the electronic devices seized from Robinson on March 14, 2025, including the drone. The drone’s flight data showed that it traveled to the location where LCI surveillance captured the inmates recovering a package. A forensic analysis of a seized cell phone revealed aerial photographs of LCI, numerous web searches related to purchasing drones, and GPS data from where the drone was launched on March 14, 2025. Investigators also found several video recordings filmed on the device, including a video that appeared to show a flight over a correctional facility, and text messages with an LCI inmate about using drones to deliver contraband to the prison and anti-drone measures used by prisons. "Correctional facilities cannot safely operate when individuals on the outside coordinate with inmates to deliver contraband over prison fences using drones,” said U.S. Attorney Bryan Stirling for the District of South Carolina. “This case sends a clear message that those who attempt to use technology to undermine prison security will be investigated, prosecuted, and held accountable for their actions.” "We are under nightly attacks by drones dropping deadly drugs and other contraband onto our prison yards," SCDC Director Joel Anderson said. "I appreciate the courts and our law enforcement partners for holding him accountable.” United States District Judge Richard M. Gergel sentenced Robinson to one year and one day in federal prison for knowingly and willfully operating an unregistered aircraft under Federal Aviation Administration laws. This case was investigated by United States Department of Transportation Office of Inspector General, the South Carolina Department of Corrections Office of Inspector General, and the Dorchester County Sheriff’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Winston Holliday prosecuted the case. ### Updated November 12, 2026 Component USAO - South Carolina

Jacksonville Pharmacy Owner and Accountant Indicted in $51 Million  Health Care Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release Jacksonville Pharmacy Owner and Accountant Indicted in $51 Million  Health Care Fraud Scheme Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Jacksonville, Florida – Charlie Bernard Griffin III (61, Jacksonville) has been charged in a 31-count federal indictment with health care fraud and money laundering. Ethelbert Chinenye Nwanegbo (47, St. Johns) has been charged in the same indictment with money laundering. Each faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison on each count. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. The indictment notifies Griffin that the United States is seeking an order of forfeiture in the amount of $14,245,474, representing Griffin’s proceeds from the health care fraud, and an order of forfeiture in the amount of $17,807,628.14, representing the property involved in the money laundering offenses with which he is charged. The indictment also notifies Griffin that the United States is seeking forfeiture of a total of $8,182,800.17 that was seized from Griffin’s bank accounts, along with three real properties and four vehicles Griffin purchased with fraud proceeds. The indictment notifies Nwanegbo that the United States is seeking an order of forfeiture in the amount of $6,068,540.50, representing the property involved in the money laundering offenses with which he is charged. According to the indictment, Griffin owned First Coast Community Development (FCCD), which operated a pharmacy in Jacksonville. Griffin entered into an agreement with a marketing company owned by Jonathan Gholston pursuant to which the company referred people to FCCD for the provision of HIV post-exposure prophylactic medications. Representatives of the marketing company set up tents and tables in Jacksonville, generally in low-income areas, and offered to provide free, government-sponsored cellphones to anyone who stopped and agreed to provide identifying information. As a result of the marketing company’s agreement with FCCD, while obtaining the personal information necessary for the person to receive the free cellphone, the marketing representatives also obtained health insurance information, including whether the person was covered by Medicare, Medicaid, or a private insurer. The agreement provided that FCCD would pay the marketing company $200 for every person who was referred for HIV medications, but that FCCD would pay this amount only if a claim submitted on behalf of the person was paid by Medicare, Medicaid, or a private insurance company. The marketing company paid its representatives a set amount, usually $50, for every person who was referred to FCCD for HIV medications, but it paid this amount only if a claim submitted on behalf of the person was paid. A marketer’s being paid per referral based upon whether a claim is paid is an illegal kickback. The information gathered by the marketing representatives was sent to FCCD and its pharmacist, Albert Chester. FCCD used the information to generate prescriptions for HIV medications that were authorized by Rashan Jones, a nurse practitioner who had never seen, spoken with, or performed any manner of evaluation, examination, or test on the persons for whom the prescriptions were issued. To ensure that FCCD’s claims for the prescriptions were paid, FCCD falsely and fraudulently used a diagnosis code reflecting that the persons to whom the prescriptions were issued had, or had been exposed to, HIV or a sexually transmitted disease, a false diagnosis that was documented in the medical records of the persons who were issued the prescriptions. FCCD filled the prescriptions, submitted claims to Medicare, Medicaid, or private insurers for the medications, and, if the claims were paid, was reimbursed for the medications. The actions of Griffin and his co-conspirators caused the submission of tens of thousands of fraudulent claims, resulting in reimbursements from Medicare, Medicaid, and private insurers totaling approximately $51 million. Griffin received a total of approximately $14 million in proceeds as a result of his involvement in the offense. Gholston, Chester, and Jones were previously charged separately and each of them agreed to plead guilty. Nwanegbo was an accountant in Jacksonville. After Griffin and a co-conspirator received proceeds of the health care fraud scheme, they transferred and deposited proceeds into accounts controlled by Nwanegbo. For some of the proceeds, Nwanegbo transferred the funds from those accounts to other accounts he controlled. Nwanegbo then returned the proceeds to Griffin and the co-conspirator by transferring and depositing the proceeds into other accounts controlled by Griffin and the co-conspirator and by making cash payments to them, after retaining a money laundering fee of approximately 10%. This case is being investigated by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services – Office of Inspector General and the Federal Bureau of Investigation. It is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Arnold B. Corsmeier. The forfeiture is being handled by Assistant United States Attorney Clint Locke. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. Updated November 12, 2026 Topics Financial Fraud Healthcare Fraud Component USAO - Florida, Middle
