title: Arizona Man Sentenced to 14 Years in Federal Prison  for Conspiracy to Distribute Controlled Substances into South Dakota
body: Press Release Arizona Man Sentenced to 14 Years in Federal Prison  for Conspiracy to Distribute Controlled Substances into South Dakota Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of South Dakota RAPID CITY - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that U.S. District Judge Camela T. Theeler has sentenced a Tucson, Arizona, man convicted of Conspiracy to Distribute a Controlled Substance.  The sentencing took place on November 9, 2026. Francisco Siquieros-Valenzuela, also known as “Pancho,” 32, was sentenced to 14 years in federal prison, followed by five years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund. Siquieros-Valenzuela was indicted for Conspiracy to Distribute a Controlled Substance by a federal grand jury in September 2025.  He pleaded guilty on May 20, 2026. The defendant was part of a multi-state drug conspiracy involving persons from Mexico, Arizona, and South Dakota responsible for importing primarily fentanyl and methamphetamine and then shipping it from Arizona to South Dakota.  Ultimately, over 1 kilogram of fentanyl pills (more than 10,000 pills) were shipped into the State. “We found this guy in Tucson,” said U.S. Attorney Parsons.  “He was sourcing fentanyl and methamphetamine out of Mexico, packaging it up, and sending it our way to poison our communities.  Let me be clear: anyone who ships illegal drugs to South Dakota, whether they ever actually set foot here or not, will be identified, tracked down, apprehended, prosecuted, and shipped off themselves to federal prison.” This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Operation Take Back America streamlines efforts and resources from the Department’s Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Forces (OCDETFs) and Project Safe Neighborhood (PSN). Through PSN, the District of South Dakota seeks to bring together all levels of law enforcement and the communities they serve to reduce gun violence and make our neighborhoods safer for everyone. This case was investigated by Drug Enforcement Administration, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Rapid City Police Department, and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives.  Criminal Chief Gregg Peterman prosecuted the case. Siquieros-Valenzuela was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service. Contact usasd.press@usdoj.gov Updated November 12, 2026 Topic Operation Take Back America Component USAO - South Dakota

title: Mission Man Sentenced to 25 Years in Federal Prison  for Second Degree Murder and Assault with a Dangerous Weapon
body: Press Release Mission Man Sentenced to 25 Years in Federal Prison  for Second Degree Murder and Assault with a Dangerous Weapon Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of South Dakota PIERRE - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that U.S. District Judge Eric C. Schulte has sentenced a Rapid City, South Dakota, man convicted of Second Degree Murder and Assault with a Dangerous Weapon.  The sentencing took place on November 9, 2026. Lucas Guerue, age 28, was sentenced to 25 years in federal prison, followed by five years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund for Second Degree Murder.  Guerue was sentenced to eight years in federal prison, followed by three years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund for Assault with a Dangerous Weapon. The sentences will be served concurrently. Guerue was indicted by a federal grand jury in May 2025 and pleaded guilty on August 13, 2026. The convictions stem from an incident that occurred within the Rosebud Sioux Indian Reservation. On March 20, 2025, sometime after 2:00 a.m., Guerue was drinking whiskey from a bottle while driving around in a Buick with a friend, when he saw the victims in a Chevrolet Traverse.  He quickly turned around and began to follow them.  Earlier that day, Guerue threatened to shoot the driver of the Traverse.  Guerue pursued the vehicle at high speeds on U.S. Highway 18 between Rosebud and Mission.  He then accelerated and intentionally rammed the back end of the Traverse at 118 miles per hour with the specific purpose of hurting its occupants.  His purpose was achieved.  The collision caused the Traverse to careen into the ditch and begin to roll.  The driver was thrown from the vehicle and killed.  The passenger was thrown from the vehicle and suffered severe injuries.  Guerue fled the scene but was later apprehended. This matter was prosecuted by the U.S. Attorney’s Office because the Major Crimes Act, a federal statute, mandates that certain violent crimes alleged to have occurred in Indian country be prosecuted in federal court as opposed to State court. This case was investigated by the Rosebud Sioux Tribe Law Enforcement Services and the Federal Bureau of Investigation.  Assistant U.S. Attorney Kimberly Zachrison prosecuted the case. Guerue was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service. Contact usasd.press@usdoj.gov Updated November 12, 2026 Topic Indian Country Law and Justice Component USAO - South Dakota

title: Austin Man Pleads Guilty to Making Violent Threats Against FBI Director and Employees
body: Press Release Austin Man Pleads Guilty to Making Violent Threats Against FBI Director and Employees Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Texas AUSTIN, Texas – An Austin man pleaded guilty in federal court this week to one count of interstate communications with threat to injure or kidnap, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas. According to court documents, June 7, Michael James Argo, 46, used the social media platform X to make several public threats to injure and murder FBI Director Kash Patel and FBI employees. An FBI agent contacted Argo about the threats on July 30. Despite being aware of the investigation into his June threats, Argo again used his X account between Sept. 13 and Sept. 18 to make additional public threats to injure, murder and kidnap Patel. A criminal complaint filed on Sept. 20 includes multiple threatening posts from Argo’s X profile. One post threatens to “kidnap and gender reassign” Patel. Other posts include photos in which Argo was brandishing a firearm. He also threatened the agent who had initially contacted him regarding the investigation based on his threats in June. Argo faces up to five years in federal prison, three years of supervised release and a maximum fine of $250,000. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. The FBI is investigating the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Britni Verdeja is prosecuting the case. ### Contact USATXW.MediaInquiry@usdoj.gov Updated November 12, 2026 Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Texas, Western

title: Jefferson County Man Sentenced to Over 21 Years in Prison for Receipt and  Possession of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Jefferson County Man Sentenced to Over 21 Years in Prison for Receipt and  Possession of Child Pornography Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov James Yerdon, age 56, of Adams Center, New York, was sentenced Monday, November 9, 2026, in federal court to 262 months in federal prison for receiving and possessing child pornography. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III, Anthony Patrone, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the Buffalo Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), and New York State Police (NYSP) Superintendent Steven G. James made the announcement. As part of his prior guilty plea, Yerdon, a previously convicted sex offender, admitted that on May 13, 2025, he possessed multiple images and videos of child pornography that he had downloaded from the internet including material depicting the sexual abuse of children as young as five months old. The defendant also possessed nude images of a 7-year-old child Yerdon had created during a trip Yerdon took with the child to the Albany, New York area. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Sarcone stated: “The defendant’s conduct in this case is horrific and is deserving of the lengthy sentence imposed today. The defendant is a repeat offender who not only sought out and accumulated child pornography online, but he also directly targeted children in our community. I am grateful to HSI and the New York State Police for their tireless work protecting our communities and especially our children from predators like the defendant.” NYSP Superintendent Steven G. James said, “Mr. Yerdon had no regard for his victims or their well-being, instead he took advantage of them in the most deplorable manner. This case serves as a reminder that those who prey on vulnerable and defenseless individuals, especially when they are in a place of trust, will be fully prosecuted. The State Police is committed to our partnership with the United States Attorney’s Office and Buffalo Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations to intercept these predators and bring an end to the damage they inflict.” In addition to the term of imprisonment, Chief U.S. District Judge, Brenda K. Sannes, also sentenced Yerdon to serve a 20-year term of supervised release, to begin after Yerdon is released from prison, at which time Yerdon will also be required to register as a sex offender. Yerdon was also ordered to pay $26,000 in restitution to victims of his offense. The case was investigated by HSI and NYSP and was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Adrian LaRochelle as part of Project Safe Childhood. Project Safe Childhood is a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys' Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . Updated November 12, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - New York, Northern

body: Press Release Rapid City Woman Sentenced to 9 Years in Federal Prison  for Conspiracy to Distribute a Controlled Substance Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of South Dakota RAPID CITY - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that U.S. District Judge Camela T. Theeler has sentenced a Rapid City, South Dakota, woman convicted of Conspiracy to Distribute a Controlled Substance.  The sentencing took place on November 10, 2026. Nicole Catches, 41, was sentenced to nine years in federal prison, followed by five years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund. Catches was indicted for Conspiracy to Distribute a Controlled Substance by a federal grand jury in October 2025 and pleaded guilty on May 18, 2026. Between July and September 2026, the defendant was a member of a conspiracy to distribute illegal drugs in Rapid City.  During the conspiracy, the defendant traveled with co-conspirators to their source of supply in Colorado.  There, they obtained a variety of illegal drugs they meant to bring back and sell in South Dakota.  In September 2026, the defendant and her co-conspirators were driving back from Colorado and were stopped by law enforcement.  When they searched the vehicle, officers found approximately 7,500 fentanyl pills, two pounds of methamphetamine, fentanyl powder, heroin, cocaine, more than $6,000 in cash, and a stolen pistol.  The defendant and her co-conspirators intended to distribute these drugs in South Dakota. This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.  Operation Take Back America streamlines efforts and resources from the Department’s Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Forces (OCDETFs) and Project Safe Neighborhood (PSN).  Through PSN, the District of South Dakota seeks to bring together all levels of law enforcement and the communities they serve to reduce gun violence and make our neighborhoods safer for everyone. This case was investigated by the Unified Narcotics Enforcement Team (UNET) and the Drug Enforcement Administration.  UNET is comprised of law enforcement officers from the Pennington County Sheriff’s Office, the Rapid City Police Department, South Dakota Division of Criminal Investigation, the South Dakota Highway Patrol and the South Dakota National Guard. Assistant U.S. Attorney Benjamin Patterson prosecuted the case. Catches was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service. Contact usasd.press@usdoj.gov Updated November 12, 2026 Topic Operation Take Back America Component USAO - South Dakota

body: Press Release Employee at Major International Law Firm Charged With Insider Trading Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of New York Defendant Repeatedly Traded in Advance of Public Announcements Related to Major Transactions Involving Law Firm’s Clients Listed on NYSE and NASDAQ Earlier today, in federal court in Brooklyn, a criminal complaint was unsealed charging Chetram Balli, also known as “Tony Balli,” with insider trading in the shares of five companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and NASDAQ.  Balli was arrested this morning in Queens, New York, and is scheduled to appear this afternoon before United States Magistrate Judge Marcia M. Henry for his initial appearance and arraignment.  As alleged in the criminal complaint, Balli misused material non-public information (MNPI) related to the law firm’s clients to trade ahead of major mergers and acquisitions.  The criminal complaint alleges that Balli made over $70,000 in profit on his trades between April 2025 and October 2026. Joseph Nocella, Jr., United States Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, and James C. Barnacle, Jr., Assistant Director in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation, New York Field Office (FBI), announced the arrest and charges. “As alleged, Balli repeatedly traded on inside information that he misappropriated from his employer and his employer’s clients,” stated United States Attorney Nocella.  “Our Office is committed to protecting the integrity of the securities markets and investors who play by the rules.  Corrupt individuals who might be tempted to take advantage of their access to confidential information should know that we are watching.” Mr. Nocella expressed his appreciation to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) Regulatory Operations – Surveillance for their significant assistance in the investigation. “Chetram Balli allegedly turned privileged access into an illegal advantage, repeatedly trading securities ahead of public announcements involving major corporate transactions.  By misappropriating confidential information for personal profit, he gained an unfair edge over law-abiding investors and compromised the fairness that our markets depend upon.  May these charges act as a warning to others, that material non-public information cannot be used for personal gain, and if it is, the FBI will follow the trail of deceit to the finish line,” stated FBI Assistant Director in Charge Barnacle. As alleged, since approximately 1989, Balli worked as a Document Processing Specialist at Law Firm-1, a major international law firm based in New York City that maintains multiple practice areas including a mergers and acquisitions practice.  As part of his employment, Balli supported attorneys by creating and revising complex legal documents, and preparing and submitting filings through the SEC’s Electronic Data gathering, Analysis and Retrieval (EDGAR) system.  Balli, who was prohibited by Law Firm-1’s policies from trading on MNPI learned in the course of his duties, used his access to non-public client information relating to upcoming partnerships, mergers, and planned acquisitions, to trade in at least five NYSE-listed or NASDAQ-listed companies. For example, as alleged in the complaint, on May 12, 2025, Balli purchased approximately 14,866 shares in E2open Parent Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: ETWO), a Texas-based provider of supply chain management software.  Balli had not previously invested in ETWO shares.  Less than two weeks later, on May 25, 2025, WiseTech Global Limited, a leading provider of software solutions for the global trade, logistics, and supply chain industries based in Australia, announced that it had entered into an agreement to acquire E2open in an all-cash transaction for $3.30 per share equating to an enterprise value of $2.1 billion.  That share price represented a 28% premium to the closing price of ETWO shares on the previous trading day.  Law Firm-1 represented WiseTech in connection with its acquisition of E2open.  Balli subsequently sold his entire ETWO position on May 27, 2025, the first trading day after the WiseTech acquisition was announced. The complaint alleged similar trading by Balli in Forge Global Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: FRGE) in advance of the November 2025 announcement of its acquisition by the Charles Schwab Corporation for $660 million; Paramount Skydance Corp. (NASDAQ: PSKY) in advance of the February 2026 announcement of its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc. for $110 billion; Talkspace, Inc. (NASDAQ: TALK) in advance of the March 2026 announcement of its acquisition by Universal Health Services, Inc. for $853 million; and Pacira BioSciences, Inc. (NYSE: PCRX) in advance of the October 2026 announcement of its acquisition by Viatris Inc. for $1.65 billion. The charges in the complaint are allegations and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.  If convicted of the charges in the complaint, Balli faces a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison. The government’s case is being handled by the Office’s Business and Securities Fraud Section.  Assistant United States  Attorneys Jonathan P. Lax and Nick M. Axelrod are in charge of the prosecution, with assistance from Paralegal Specialist Melina Piatti-Chayan. The Defendant : CHETRAM BALLI Age:  54 Hollis, Queens E.D.N.Y. Docket No. 26-MJ-204 Contact John Marzulli Denise Taylor United States Attorney’s Office (718) 254-6323 Updated November 12, 2026 Topics Financial Fraud Securities, Commodities, & Investment Fraud Component USAO - New York, Eastern

Man Who Allegedly Trafficked Cocaine in Chicago Arrested in Argentina and Extradited to United States
body: Press Release Man Who Allegedly Trafficked Cocaine in Chicago Arrested in Argentina and Extradited to United States Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Illinois CHICAGO — A man who allegedly trafficked cocaine in Chicago has been arrested in Argentina and extradited to the United States to face federal drug conspiracy charges in the Northern District of Illinois. RODOLFO AGUIRRE, 38, was originally arrested in Chicago in December 2016 after allegedly conspiring to sell approximately 7,000 grams of cocaine outside of a hotel in the city’s Uptown neighborhood, according to a criminal complaint filed in federal court in Chicago. Unbeknownst to Aguirre, the buyer was an undercover law enforcement agent, the complaint states.  Aguirre was released on bond conditions, but he failed to appear in federal court ahead of his scheduled trial in 2017. Aguirre was recently arrested in Argentina and extradited to the United States last week.  He is scheduled to appear in federal court in Chicago on Nov. 17, 2026, at 10:15 a.m., before U.S. District Judge John J. Tharp, Jr.  The government will be seeking Aguirre’s continued detention pending trial. The charges and extradition were announced by Andrew S. Boutros, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois, and Todd C. Smith, Special Agent-in-Charge of the Chicago Field Division of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration.  The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael Spitulnik. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs worked with the Government of Argentina to secure the Nov. 6, 2026, extradition of Aguirre. The public is reminded that charges are not evidence of guilt.  The defendant is presumed innocent and entitled to a fair trial at which the government has the burden of proving guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. aguirre_et_al_indictment.pdf aguirre_et_al_complaint.pdf Updated November 12, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Components Criminal - Office of International Affairs Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) USAO - Illinois, Northern

title: Mableton Man Faces Federal Charges After Agents Seize Nearly 60 Pounds of Fentanyl from Backyard Shed
body: Press Release Mableton Man Faces Federal Charges After Agents Seize Nearly 60 Pounds of Fentanyl from Backyard Shed Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Georgia Atlanta – Michael Antonio Cruz was arraigned earlier today in federal court on drug trafficking charges related to the discovery of nearly 60 pounds of fentanyl in a shed behind one of his alleged residences. “The staggering quantity of fentanyl Cruz allegedly possessed posed a critical threat to public health and safety. But for the intervention of law enforcement, the fentanyl could have reached the streets and had potentially fatal consequences,” said U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg. “My office will continue to work closely with our law enforcement partners to aggressively prosecute the criminals who deal this poison in our community.” “Fentanyl continues to devastate families and communities across this country,” said Michael J. Connolly, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the DEA Atlanta Field Division. “The alleged trafficking of 60 pounds of this deadly substance underscores the magnitude of the threat we face. DEA will continue to pursue those responsible for putting profits over human lives. Our mission remains dedicated to protecting our communities, preventing drug trafficking, and working toward a Fentanyl Free America.” According to U.S. Attorney Hertzberg, the charges, and other information presented in court: On September 30, 2026, federal agents conducting a narcotics investigation executed search warrants at three residences allegedly owned by Cruz. In Austell, Georgia, agents searched a backyard shed and found nearly 60 pounds of fentanyl shaped in 26 individually wrapped bricks with stamped markings on each side. In a Mableton, Georgia residence, agents found multiple scales, buckets of a cutting agent commonly used with methamphetamine and cocaine, plastic bins containing methamphetamine residue, vacuum sealing machines, and vacuum sealing packages. Agents also found a false vent that opened into a void in the wall, where they discovered more than $74,000 in cash. Today, Michael Antonio Cruz, 32, of Mableton, Georgia, was arraigned in federal court on an indictment returned by a grand jury on November 3, 2026, that charged him with conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine and fentanyl as well as possession with intent to distribute fentanyl. Cruz was ordered detained in the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service pending further proceedings. Members of the public are reminded that the indictment only contains charges. The defendant is presumed innocent of the charges, and it will be the government’s burden to prove the defendant’s guilt beyond a reasonable doubt at trial. This case is being investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration, with valuable assistance provided by the Cobb County Police Department, Cobb County Sheriff’s Office, and Homeland Security Investigations. Assistant United States Attorney Edward C. Robinson Jr. is prosecuting the case. This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. The U.S. Attorney’s Office in Atlanta recommends parents and children learn about the dangers of drugs at the following web site: www.justthinktwice.gov . For further information please contact the U.S. Attorney’s Public Affairs Office at USAGAN.PressEmails@usdoj.gov or (404) 581-6185. The Internet address for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia is http://www.justice.gov/usao-ndga . Updated November 12, 2026 Topics Operation Take Back America Drug Trafficking Components Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) USAO - Georgia, Northern

title: Pair who led retail theft conspiracy to be arraigned for $5.6 million in theft from four retailers
body: Press Release Pair who led retail theft conspiracy to be arraigned for $5.6 million in theft from four retailers Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Washington Defendants allegedly collected more than $3 million selling stolen goods to consumers, third-party resellers, and wholesalers Seattle – Two men who allegedly led a sophisticated scheme to steal and resell products from four online retailers will be arraigned tomorrow on a three-count indictment that outlined the multi-million-dollar fraud scheme, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd. Brian Vinh Pham of 29, of Arlington, Texas, and Romar Aragon Noto, 22, of North Hills, California, will be arraigned on the indictment tomorrow at 11:00 AM in U.S. District Court in Seattle. According to the indictment, between April 2023, and February 2026, Pham and Noto led a sophisticated retail theft ring that transported stolen property across the country, including into the Western District of Washington. The men stole the merchandise by exploiting return policies and obtaining fraudulent refunds.  For one retailer, they also exploited a glitch on the retailer’s website to obtain more than 55,000 pieces of merchandise without payment. They then sold the stolen goods directly to consumers, to other third-party resellers, and to wholesalers. The indictment details how Pham and Noto’s group targeted four retailers to obtain more than $3.2 million worth of goods by obtaining fraudulent refunds. After ordering the merchandise, they would initiate returns with retailers who paid refunds when the return shipping labels were scanned.  The theft ring used a variety of tactics to show the return packages were shipped but never actually returned the stolen goods. During a five-month period, a retailer of home improvement goods, Retailer 2, paid $124,000 in refunds to Pham and Noto’s group for over 200 expander tools, only to have the return labels affixed to empty envelopes or boxes. Pham and Noto sold expander tools via Amazon Marketplace for $96,000. Similarly, during a 10-month period, the co-conspirators ordered and obtained more than $162,000 in refunds for more than 350 tankless water heaters that they failed to return. About 297 of the water heaters were sold on Amazon Marketplace for more than $181,000. In total, that victim was defrauded of more than 2,800 items valued at more than $1.4 million. Retailer 3, a clothing retailer, was defrauded of 15,000 pieces of clothing worth over $1 million. The clothes were sold in bulk to other third-party resellers. Retailer 4 was defrauded of clothing worth $767,000 in some 900 orders where a refund was claimed but the goods were not returned.  Retailer 1, a manufacturer of insulated stainless-steel tumblers, issued refunds totaling more than $53,000 for over 1,000 tumblers that were never returned. Pham and Noto’s group also targeted Retailer 1 when its website had a glitch that canceled bulk orders but then still fulfilled and shipped some canceled orders without payment.  The pair’s group used the messaging platform Discord to coordinate placing more than 7,000 orders, seeking to obtain more than 150,000 tumblers valued at about $6.5 million.  The group successfully stole more than 55,000 tumblers worth approximately $2.4 million through 2,700 orders.  Pham and Noto used warehouses in Texas and California to store the enormous inventory before selling the tumblers on Amazon Marketplace, to third-party resellers, and to wholesalers. The co-conspirators set up various business entities and bank accounts to execute their scheme. Both men are charged with money laundering for transferring their ill-gotten proceeds from one of their business accounts to another account. Conspiracy to commit interstate transportation of stolen property is punishable by up to five years in prison. Money laundering is punishable by up to ten years in prison. The charges contained in the indictment are only allegations.  A person is presumed innocent unless and until he or she is proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. The case is being investigated by the FBI. pham_noto_indictment.pdf Contact Press contact for the U.S. Attorney’s Office is Communications Director Emily Langlie at (206) 553-4110 or Emily.Langlie@usdoj.gov . Updated November 12, 2026 Topic Fraud Component USAO - Washington, Western

title: Coralville Man Sentenced to Over 11 Years in Federal Prison for Firearm and Receipt of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Coralville Man Sentenced to Over 11 Years in Federal Prison for Firearm and Receipt of Child Pornography Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Iowa DAVENPORT, Iowa – A Coralville, Iowa man was sentenced on November 12, 2026, to 140 months in federal prison for two counts of possession of an unregistered firearm and one count of receipt of child pornography. According to public court documents and evidence presented at sentencing, Edward Ian Whitehouse, also known as Kodi, 59, received numerous images and videos containing child sexual abuse material, including content with minors as young as infancy. Whitehouse messaged self-purported minors and made plans for the self-purported minors to travel to Iowa to meet with him and engaged in sex acts. Whitehouse was found to be in possession of numerous weapons and ammunition, including four rifles, two shotguns, two handguns, 15 different firearm magazines, an AR-15 rifle with a silencer attached, and a separate a rifle silencer. Neither silencer was registered to Whitehouse under the National Firearms Registration and Transfer Record. After completing his term of imprisonment, Whitehouse will be required to serve an eight-year term of supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system. Whitehouse was also ordered to pay $12,000 in restitution. United States Attorney David C. Waterman of the Southern District of Iowa made the announcement. The Coralville Police Department, Joint Forensic Analysis Cyber Team, and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives investigated the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. For more information about Project Safe Neighborhoods, please visit Justice.gov/PSN. Contact MacKenzie Tubbs Public Information Officer 515-473-9300 USAIAS.PAO@usdoj.gov Updated November 12, 2026 Topics Project Safe Childhood Project Safe Neighborhoods Firearms Offenses Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - Iowa, Southern

title: International Law Enforcement Operation Targeting Opioid and Fentanyl Traffickers on the Dark Web Results in over 350 Arrests Worldwide and the Seizure of Drugs, Weapons, and over $234 Million
body: Press Release International Law Enforcement Operation Targeting Opioid and Fentanyl Traffickers on the Dark Web Results in over 350 Arrests Worldwide and the Seizure of Drugs, Weapons, and over $234 Million Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Largest Takedown in JCODE’s History of Dark Web Narcotics Vendors Who Sold to Tens of Thousands of U.S. Residents Note: Relevant court documents can be found here . Today, the Department of Justice, through the Joint Criminal Opioid and Darknet Enforcement (JCODE) team, joined Europol to announce the results of Operation TorNado: a coordinated, multi‑agency and international law enforcement effort targeting criminal enterprises that use Dark Web markets to traffic fentanyl, opioids, and other illicit drugs. The operation, which was conducted across the United States, Europe, Australia and New Zealand, demonstrates the continued partnership between JCODE and Europol against the illegal sale of drugs and other illicit goods and services on the Dark Web. Operation TorNado represents the sixth — and most extensive — internationally coordinated action since JCODE was created in 2018 and builds on the success of last year’s Operation RapTor . This operation included actions against Dark Web vendors and buyers who were active on prominent Dark Web drug markets seized by law enforcement including: Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom, and Tor2Door. “Nothing will stop the Trump Administration from identifying and dismantling drug trafficking networks,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Thanks to our partnerships with state, federal, and international law enforcement through the Joint Criminal Opioid and Darknet Enforcement (JCODE) team, Operation TorNado crippled Dark Web market vendors and will bring alleged drug traffickers to justice. The Department of Justice will continue protecting the American people from lethal synthetic drugs and identifying bad actors around the globe who threaten American lives.” Following the takedown of multiple darknet marketplaces and vendor targets in the previous JCODE operation, U.S. and international law enforcement agencies obtained intelligence to identify Dark Web drug traffickers, resulting in a series of complementary, but separate, law enforcement investigations. Operation TorNado actions have resulted in the arrest of 354 Dark Web drug traffickers and fraudulent criminals who engaged in tens of thousands of sales of illicit goods and services across the United States, Europe, Australia, and New Zealand. This operation resulted in the seizure of over $234 million in both cash and virtual currencies; approximately 5.7 metric tons of illicit drugs worldwide, including fentanyl and other opioids, methamphetamine, heroin, cocaine, ecstasy, and MDMA, 38 pill presses; and 209 firearms. Dark Web vendor accounts were identified and attributed to real individuals selling illicit goods on Dark Web markets such as DrugHub, Archetyp, and others. By leveraging complementary partnerships and surging resources across the U.S. government and Europol, Operation TorNado significantly disrupted the online opioid trade and sends a strong message that criminals operating on the Dark Web are not beyond the reach of law enforcement. Operation TorNado led to 132 arrests in the United States, two in Australia, six in Austria, four in Czechia, one in Finland, 23 in France, 41 in Germany, 45 in Hungary, five in Ireland, 12 in the Netherlands, 13 in New Zealand, 11 in Slovenia, and 59 in the United Kingdom (UK). A number of investigations are still ongoing to identify the individuals behind Dark Web accounts. “Operation TorNado is the largest interagency takedown of Dark Web drug vendors and buyers to date, resulting in 354 arrests worldwide, including 132 in the United States,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “Through the coordinated effort, this FBI and our partners collectively seized 5.7 metric tons of illicit drugs, including deadly fentanyl, as well as $234 million in cryptocurrency and cash. This FBI continues to accelerate our cyber capabilities including through our newly established Cyber Branch, evolving how we operate to meet the dynamic threat landscape presented by the Dark Web. The success of the Operation TorNado makes clear that criminals cannot hide behind technology or geography – no matter where you operate, justice will find you. Thank you to our JCODE and Homeland Security Task Force partners who continue to do elite work defending the homeland.” “Drug traffickers are exploiting the dark web to distribute fentanyl and other deadly drugs into American communities, profiting from addiction and overdose deaths,” said Administrator Terrance Cole of the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). “Operation TorNado demonstrates the strength of JCODE and our international law enforcement partnerships. DEA, working as part of the Homeland Security Task Force through our field offices, played a significant role in identifying these criminals, exposing their trafficking networks, and disrupting their operations. Whether they operate on the streets or behind anonymous online accounts, DEA will use every available investigative tool to dismantle these organizations and bring those responsible to justice.” “Operation TorNado demonstrates the power of global partnership and underscores a vital truth: when the international law enforcement community stands united, borders offer no sanctuary to criminals,” said U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) Chief Postal Inspector Gary Barksdale. “No matter where criminals attempt to hide, the U.S. Postal Inspection Service and our partners around the world will pursue them, dismantle their networks, and bring them to justice. Our commitment to protecting the public and holding these criminals accountable remains unwavering.” “The dark web is not a safe haven for criminals,” said Acting Executive Associate Director John A. Condon of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI). “This operation demonstrates what happens when law enforcement agencies around the world combine their intelligence, resources and expertise to dismantle criminal networks. With 354 arrests, more than five tons of drugs seized, and hundreds of millions of dollars in criminal assets taken out of circulation, we’ve sent a clear message: Criminals can operate in the shadows, but they can’t hide from justice.” “Criminal networks may operate across borders and in the shadows of the Dark Web, but they cannot operate without money,” said Chief Jarod Koopman of IRS Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI). “IRS-CI is a global leader in financial crime investigations because our special agents have the expertise and international reach to follow the money, unravelling even the most complex schemes and exposing the people behind them. Operation TorNado demonstrates the power of combining financial intelligence with strong international law enforcement partnerships to disrupt illicit markets, seize criminal proceeds and hold traffickers accountable.” “The sale of illegal drugs through darknet marketplaces carries real and often tragic consequences for consumers and communities alike,” said Assistant Commissioner Justin Green of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Office of Criminal Investigations. “The FDA is steadfast in its commitment to identifying, investigating, and holding accountable those who use these platforms to traffic in dangerous drugs at the expense of public health.” The extensive operation, which spanned from May 2025 to October 2026, resulted in dozens of federal prosecutions including: Stanislav Chernyshov, 30, a Russian national illegally residing in the United States, and his brother Vladislav Chernyshov, 35, a naturalized U.S. citizen, were arrested in Florida for allegedly operating Dark Web vendor “BarbaraWhite,” which sold counterfeit oxycodone M30 pills laced with highly potent nitazenes, synthetic opioids that can equal or surpass fentanyl’s potency. Lab analyses, covert purchases, and surveillance tied the brothers to a clandestine pill‑manufacturing and nationwide mailing operation allegedly responsible for over one thousand parcels shipped across 49 states, with multiple fatal and non-fatal overdoses identified among recipients of their products. They are charged with conspiracy to distribute Schedule I synthetic opioids in the Eastern District of Virginia. If convicted, they each face a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. Alexander Green, 32, a U.S. citizen of Jacksonville, North Carolina, and formerly of Hazlet, New Jersey, was arrested in June for operating the STARLABS Cyber-Enabled Drug Trafficking Organization (DTO), an online vendor responsible for distributing a wide array of illicit narcotics - including fentanyl - on the Monero-only Dark Web market Drughub. Operating under the moniker “STARLABS,” Green’s DTO has been linked to two overdose deaths in the Southern District of Ohio. The June 2026 enforcement action resulted in the seizure of approximately 200 grams of methamphetamine and more than two kilograms of counterfeit pharmaceutical pills with fentanyl present. Green is charged in the Southern District of Ohio with conspiracy to distribute and possess with intent to distribute controlled substances and distribution of controlled substances (fentanyl and methamphetamine). If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. Jonatan Gonzales, 35, a U.S. citizen of South Bakersfield, California, was arrested after he was identified as a Dark Web narcotics vendor “SpeedyPharma” who was shipping methamphetamine, as well as black tar heroin, cocaine, and K2 paper, to multiple addresses in western Pennsylvania, as well as to all other 49 states. Gonzales is charged with possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine in the Western District of Pennsylvania. U.S. law enforcement seized 48 lbs. of methamphetamine, 588 grams of cocaine, 386 grams of black tar heroin, 3.5 grams of fentanyl, 2.8 grams of carfentanil, and $40,565 in cash following a search of his residence. If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of life in prison. Michael Morales, 25, of Bergenfield, New Jersey; Thomas A. Crisafulli, 27, of Bergenfield, Naudy Oviedo, 21, of Bronx, New York; Jayshawn Eyamazememba, 22, of Bronx, and Ethan Lara, 25, of Lodi, New Jersey, were arrested in New Jersey for their alleged roles in a New York/New Jersey distribution cell operating on behalf of a nationwide drug trafficking organization that distributed counterfeit Xanax, MDMA, ketamine, and other controlled substances through a nationwide mail-based distribution network. During the investigation, law enforcement executed search warrants at multiple locations and seized approximately 300 kilograms of counterfeit Xanax, MDMA, ketamine, and other controlled substances from a residence in Lodi, New Jersey, a storage unit in Lawrence Township, New Jersey, and other locations in Bergenfield and Englewood, New Jersey. The defendants were charged in Bergen County, New Jersey, with maintaining or operating a controlled dangerous substance production facility, manufacturing, distributing, or possessing with intent to distribute a controlled dangerous substance, and manufacturing, distributing, or possessing with intent to distribute marijuana or hashish. If convicted, they face a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. The Bergen County Prosecutor's Office is handling the prosecution. Eric Turner, 30, of Lizella, Georgia, and Jose Smith, 29, of Valrico, Florida, both U.S. citizens, were arrested in June for operating a sophisticated Dark Web DTO primarily selling bulk quantities of heroin and fentanyl using the monikers Postmates and FuegoPacksXpress. Turner and Smith are charged with conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute heroin in the Middle District of Florida. U.S. law enforcement seized 4.5 kilograms of heroin, 22 grams of fentanyl, MDMA and alprazolam tablets and 25 firearms following a search of their residences. If convicted, they face a maximum penalty of life in prison. Operation TorNado was a collaborative initiative across JCODE members, including the Department of Justice; FBI; DEA; FDA Office of Criminal Investigations; HSI; IRS-CI; USPIS; Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF); Army Criminal Investigation Division (Army-CID); U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP); Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN); Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC); and Naval Criminal Investigative Service (NCIS). Local, state and other federal agencies also contributed to Operation TorNado investigations. The investigations leading to Operation TorNado were significantly aided by essential support and coordination by the Criminal Division’s Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section; Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section, the Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs, the International Computer Hacking and Intellectual Property (ICHIP) prosecutor based in The Hague, Europol and its Dark Web team and international partners Eurojust, Australian Federal Police (AFP), Austria’s Criminal Intelligence Service with various Provincial Criminal Police Offices (Bundeskriminalamt und Landeskriminalämter); Czechia’s National Drug Headquarters - Criminal Police and Investigation Service (Národní protidrogová centrála SKPV PČR); General Directorate of Customs (Generální ředitelství cel); Finland’s Finnish Customs (Tulli); France’s National Gendarmerie (Gendarmerie Nationale); Germany’s Federal Criminal Police Office (Bundeskriminalamt); General Prosecutor’s Office in Frankfurt/Main, Central Office for Combating Cybercrime, Prosecutor’s Office in Cologne – Central Cybercrime Contact Point (Staatsanwaltschaft Köln, Zentral- und Ansprechstelle Cybercrime); Central Criminal Investigation in Oldenburg (Zentrale Kriminalinspektion Oldenburg); various police departments (Dienststellen der Länderpolizeien); German Customs Investigation (Zollfahndungsämter); Hungary’s National Bureau of Investigation and several police departments (Nemzeti Nyomozó Iroda); Ireland’s Garda National Cyber Crime Bureau (An Garda Síochána); Montenegro’s Police Directorate of Montenegro (Uprava policije Crne Gore); Netherlands Team High Tech Crime (National Investigations and Special Operations (NIS) and Post Interventie Team (PIT); National Intelligence, Expertise and Operational Support (NIEO); New Zealand’s Police (Ngā Pirihimana o Aotearoa); Slovenia’s Illicit Drugs Section in Criminal Police Directorate (Uprava kriminalistične policije), General Police Directorate in cooperation with the Criminal Police Directorate in Maribor (Policijska uprava Maribor) and the UK’s National Crime Agency (NCA) and National Police Chiefs’ Council (NPCC). Federal prosecutions are being conducted in more than 20 federal districts, including: the Central District of California, the Eastern District of California, the Northern District of California, the Southern District of California, the District of Colorado, the District of Columbia, the District of Connecticut, the Middle District of Florida, the Southern District of Florida, the Northern District of Georgia, the Middle District of Georgia, the Northern District of Illinois, the Northern District of Indiana, the Eastern District of Kentucky, the District of Maryland, the District of Massachusetts, the Western District of Michigan, the Eastern District of Missouri, the Western District of Missouri, the District of Nebraska, the District of New Jersey, the Southern District of New York, the Northern District of Ohio, the Southern District of Ohio, the Eastern District of Pennsylvania, the Western District of Pennsylvania, the District of Puerto Rico, the District of Rhode Island, the Eastern District of Texas, the Northern District of Texas, the Eastern District of Virginia, and the Western District of Wisconsin. JCODE is an FBI-led Department of Justice initiative to disrupt global drug‑trafficking networks and the digital infrastructure that enables them. Operation TorNado illustrates the investigative power of federal and international partnerships to combat the borderless nature of online criminal activity. The Justice Department is providing intellectual property and cybercrime technical assistance to foreign law enforcement, prosecutorial, and judicial partners in other countries through the ICHIP program. The Criminal Division’s ICHIP Program is jointly administered by the Criminal Division’s Office of Overseas Prosecutorial Development, Assistance and Training (OPDAT) and the Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section through partnership between the U.S. Department of State’s Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs. title: New York Doctor Charged in $6.8M Medicare Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release New York Doctor Charged in $6.8M Medicare Fraud Scheme Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs A federal grand jury in the Southern District of Florida returned an indictment on Tuesday charging Dr. Edgard Salazar, 57, of Armonk, New York, with conspiring to bill Medicare for thousands of consultations that never occurred and millions of dollars of orthotic braces that Medicare patients did not want or need. According to court documents, telemedicine company TelevisitMD allegedly allowed Salazar to sign pre-filled prescriptions for Medicare beneficiaries who did not need the orthotic braces ordered in the prescriptions. Salazar did not examine or treat the beneficiaries and often did not speak to them at all. At times, when Salazar did speak to the beneficiaries, they told Salazar they did not want or need orthotic braces. Salazar signed prescriptions for them anyway. Salazar also billed Medicare for telemedicine consultations that he never performed. Salazar allegedly participated in submitting over $6.8 million in false and fraudulent claims to Medicare. Christopher Harwood owned and operated TelevisitMD. In March 2026, Harwood pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit health care fraud and wire fraud and agreed to pay $17.9 million in restitution. Last month, Harwood was sentenced to 20 years in prison for his role in the conspiracy. Salazar is charged with conspiracy to commit health care fraud and five counts of health care fraud. If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison on each count. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division; Special Agent in Charge Brett Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office; and Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda Bennett of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG) made the announcement. FBI and HHS-OIG investigated the case. Trial Attorney Owen Dunn of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section is prosecuting the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at https://www.justice.gov/fraud/health-care-fraud-section . An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Updated November 12, 2026 Topic Fraud Component National Fraud Enforcement Division Press Release Number: 26-1352

title: Gootloader Malware Disrupted in International Cyber Operation
body: Press Release Gootloader Malware Disrupted in International Cyber Operation Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Colorado USACO.PublicAffairs@usdoj.gov DENVER — The Department of Justice today announced the successful removal of malware known as “Gootloader” from over 100 computer servers, including compromised WordPress sites, and the seizure of U.S. domain names used by criminals to deliver and control the Gootloader malware. Since 2018, Gootloader malware has infected at least 25,000 computers around the world. Gootloader malware has been used in ransomware attacks of at least 44 U.S. based victims which has resulted in approximately $28.8 million in loss. “With court authorization, the Department of Justice and FBI, along with our international partners, conducted an online operation that liberated over 100 servers from malicious software, denying ransomware criminals a platform,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “The Department of Justice has, once again, advanced President Trump’s Cyber Strategy by disrupting criminals’ cyber infrastructure.” “Cybercrime knows no borders and this case is an excellent example of international partnerships working to protect people around the world,” said U.S. Attorney Peter McNeilly for the District of Colorado. “I am proud of the role we played in disrupting this botnet and thank our partners for their exceptional work to unearth this complex network.” “The Gootloader malware targeted victims on a global scale, including attacks on the U.S. Department of War and the Defense Industrial Base,” said Special Agent in Charge Kenneth DeChellis of the Department of War, formerly known as the Department of Defense, Office of Inspector General Defense Criminal Investigative Service (DCIS), Cyber Field Office. “This announcement is a testament to the long-standing partnership and shared resolve between international law enforcement and private-sector organizations in pursuing cyber threats.” “Using a network of compromised websites, Gootloader malware infected thousands of computers worldwide, providing cybercriminals with access to deploy ransomware and cause millions of dollars in losses,” said Operations Director Brett Leatherman of the FBI Cyber Branch. “Working alongside our partners, we disrupted the Gootloader botnet through coordinated technical operations, victim notifications, and remediation. Strong international and private-sector partnerships made this disruption possible, allowing us to protect victims from further harm and prevent future exploitation.” “Dismantling the Gootloader malware and botnet, which infected over 25,000 systems worldwide, demonstrates the power of unified, international law enforcement operations,” said Director L. Scott Moreland, Department of the Army Criminal Investigation Division. “Alongside our global partners, Army CID is committed to taking the fight directly to cybercriminals. While disrupting these criminal networks stops ransomware attacks before they can take root, true cyber resilience relies on a combination of global law enforcement action and everyday personal vigilance.” According to warrants unsealed this week, Gootloader is malware that infects victim computers through a variety of means, often by tricking unsuspecting individuals into downloading it. Once infected, the compromised computers are added to a network of other compromised computers known as a botnet. The actors behind Gootloader used the botnet to infect other computers, then sell access to those later-infected computers to ransomware actors. In addition to the law enforcement seizures, the Shadowserver Foundation assisted by working with internet service providers and Computer Security Incident Response Teams (CSIRTs) to identify infected systems, aid in notifying victims and assisting in remediation. Visitors to the seized domains will see the following seizure banner: These actions were conducted in coordination with Operation Endgame, a multinational law enforcement initiative targeting the dismantling of malware cybercriminal services. More information regarding Operation Endgame can be found at www.operation-endgame.com . The Gootloader investigation was led by DCIS, FBI’s Denver Field Office and the Army Criminal Investigative Division, working closely with Germany’s Bundeskriminalamt (BKA), the Netherlands National Police’s National High Tech Crime Unit, Canada’s Royal Canadian Mounted Police and Ottawa Police Service, Danish Police, Brigade de Lutte contre la cybercriminalité (Paris Cybercrime Unit), United Kindom’s National Crime Agency, the Australian Federal Police and Europol. ICHIP the Hague, Fraunhofer FKIE, Registrar of Last Resort (RoLR), OpenAI and Sharktech, Inc. also provided valuable technical assistance to the investigation. Senior Counsel Thomas Dougherty of the Criminal Division’s Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section (CCIPS) and Assistant U.S. Attorney Jasand Mock for the District of Colorado are prosecuting the case. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs also provided valuable assistance. CCIPS investigates and prosecutes cybercrime and intellectual property (IP) crime in coordination with domestic and international law enforcement agencies, often with assistance from the private sector. Since 2020, CCIPS has secured the conviction of over 220 cyber and IP criminals, and court orders for the return of over $500 million in victim funds. The Justice Department is providing IP and cybercrime technical assistance to foreign law enforcement, prosecutorial, and judicial partners in other countries through the ICHIP program. The Criminal Division’s ICHIP Program is jointly administered by the Criminal Division’s Office of Overseas Prosecutorial Development, Assistance and Training (OPDAT) and CCIPS through partnership between the U.S. Department of State’s Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs. Contact USACO.PublicAffairs@usdoj.gov Updated November 12, 2026 Component USAO - Colorado

title: Wheeling Man Sentenced for Selling Drugs in Public Housing
body: Press Release Wheeling Man Sentenced for Selling Drugs in Public Housing Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of West Virginia WHEELING, WEST VIRGINIA – A Wheeling, West Virginia man was sentenced to a decade in prison for trafficking drugs from a public housing apartment, announced U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey. Roger Lee Williams, Jr., 32, was sentenced to 120 months in federal prison. Following a few sales of cocaine to a confidential informant, investigators executed a search warrant at the Booker T. Apartments where Williams lived. Officers seized cocaine and methamphetamine and found $3,040 from Williams. Williams has a criminal history that includes domestic violence, drug trafficking, larceny, obstruction, and fleeing. Assistant U.S. Attorney Clayton Reid prosecuted the case on behalf of the government. The Ohio Valley Drug Task Force, a HIDTA-funded initiative; the Drug Enforcement Administration; and the Ohio County Sheriff’s Office investigated. This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime, and repel the invasion of illegal immigration. U.S. District Judge John Preston Bailey presided. Updated November 12, 2026 Topics Operation Take Back America Drug Trafficking Component USAO - West Virginia, Northern

title: Federal jury convicts Lubbock man of methamphetamine distribution and firearm offenses
body: Press Release Federal jury convicts Lubbock man of methamphetamine distribution and firearm offenses Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas LUBBOCK, Texas — U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a 36-year-old Lubbock man was convicted on Nov. 10 of drug and gun charges following a multi-agency search warrant at his residence in January. Following a two-day trial presided over by U.S. District Judge James Wesley Hendrix, a federal jury took less than two hours to convict Jarrod Charles Gauna on all three counts charged in a May indictment. The convictions included conspiracy to distribute and possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine, possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine, and possession of firearms in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. ”The defendant chose to distribute dangerous drugs and carry a firearm in furtherance of that criminal activity. A jury held him accountable, and he now faces the possibility of spending the rest of his life in federal prison,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “Our office will never waver in its commitment to prosecuting those who profit by poisoning our communities, fueling addiction, and taking away the freedom and dignity of others. We will continue to use every lawful tool available to protect the public and deliver justice for the people of this district.” “Drug trafficking and its frequent companion, drug-related violence, place the safety of our communities at serious risk,” said DEA Dallas Special Agent in Charge Joseph B. Tucker. “This guilty verdict ensures Mr. Gauna is held accountable for his criminal actions, taking dangerous drugs and ready-to-use firearms off our streets before they can cause further harm and has undoubtedly saved lives.” According to evidence presented at trial, Lubbock Police Department and Drug Enforcement Administration narcotics agents became aware of Gauna’s residence in west Lubbock after it was involved in two different drug controlled purchases. During the first purchase in October 2025, Gauna’s codefendant, John Deleon, traveled to Gauna’s residence just prior to meeting with a confidential informant and delivering several ounces of methamphetamine. Deleon followed the same pattern before delivering additional methamphetamine to an informant in November 2025. Deleon pled guilty to methamphetamine distribution charges in August. On Jan. 15, narcotics agents executed a search warrant at Gauna’s residence.  Agents found approximately one-half ounce of methamphetamine along with several ounces of dimethyl sulfone, also known as MSM. The jury heard evidence that MSM is a substance that drug traffickers commonly use to “cut” methamphetamine to increase the quantity that can be sold. The jury also heard evidence that this same cutting agent was present in the methamphetamine that Deleon delivered to the informant during the controlled purchases. Agents also found four firearms in Gauna’s residence—three pistols and one over-under shotgun. All three pistols were loaded and readily accessible. One was located within inches of the drug evidence and the other two were in or near Gauna’s bedroom. A DEA drug trafficking expert explained the violence inherent in methamphetamine trafficking and how firearms such as these are used to protect drug dealers from being robbed. Gauna admitted to narcotics agents that the guns and drugs belonged to him. He also had several empty, unused baggies in his pocket. Witnesses testified that these baggies are commonly used to package methamphetamine for distribution. Gauna now faces up to life in federal prison. Because Gauna has a previous conviction for possessing a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime, he faces an enhanced minimum sentence of 25 years imprisonment following his second such conviction. Any sentence he receives for the drug charges must also run consecutively to the firearm charge. Gauna’s sentencing is scheduled for March 4, 2027. The Drug Enforcement Administration and Lubbock Police Department led this investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Sean Long and Tyler Smotherman are prosecuting the case. Contact Public Affairs Division U.S. Attorney’s Office Northern District of Texas USATXN.Media@usdoj.gov Updated November 12, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Texas, Northern

title: Big Stone Gap Man Pleads Guilty to Illegal Possession of a Firearm
body: Press Release Big Stone Gap Man Pleads Guilty to Illegal Possession of a Firearm Thursday, November 12, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Virginia ABINGDON, Va. – A Big Stone Gap man, with a history of drug distribution, pled guilty last week to illegally possessing a firearm as a previously convicted felon. Jeremy Michael Boggs, 45, pled guilty last week to one count of possessing a firearm after having been convicted of a felony. Boggs has agreed to be sentenced to a term of imprisonment between eight and twelve years. According to court documents, on January 7, 2026, law enforcement received a call for trespassing at an apartment building in Wise, Virginia. Upon arriving at the scene, officers located Boggs in the laundry room of the apartment building and learned Boggs had an outstanding warrant for his arrest. As officers searched Boggs pursuant to his arrest on the outstanding warrant, an officer located an empty holster on Boggs’s belt. Wrapped inside a jacket Boggs had been wearing, officers found a loaded, Smith and Wesson revolver. In one of the jacket pockets, officers found a bag containing nine additional rounds of ammunition. Boggs was prohibited from possessing firearms due to at least four previous felony convictions in Virginia and Tennessee, including for drug distribution and aggravated assault. First Assistant United States Attorney Robert N. Tracci and Anthony Spotswood, Special Agent in Charge, ATF Washington Division, made the announcement made the announcement. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, Wise Police Department, and Wise County Sheriff’s Office investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Corey Hall is prosecuting the case. Updated November 12, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Virginia, Western
